   132	  state. If both reviewers are automated, they use different model families;
   133	  otherwise at least one reviewer is human. Sanitized prompt and reviewer
   134	  identity hashes are recorded without credentials or secret material.
   135	- Each pass records at least 12 concrete falsification attempts, including
   136	  attempted violations that the suite correctly catches. Findings cite exact
   137	  evidence and are independently reproduced before any fix.
   138	- Zero verified findings may remain unresolved. False positives remain recorded
   139	  with reproduction evidence; they are not silently deleted.

   163	  replayability, traceability, and fault coverage instead of test count alone.

   169	  suite automatically.

   174	  branch coverage does not show that assertions detect semantic defects.

   176	  cannot be repeated on a review schedule and termination becomes subjective.
   177	- **Broad source-wide mutation testing** — rejected because utility-code mutants
   178	  inflate cost and score while diluting critical contract coverage.

    12	# R-003 — the verifier is not traced by itself
    13	
    14	**Finding ruled on.** Blind pass 2 at lane base `5fb1b57`, attempt A07 (corpus

    16	access audit only covers the qualification lane stages, not the verifier

    20	verifier that judges those traces runs outside them.
    21	
    22	**Ruling.** This is class C under AM-17.9: closing it requires the gate to be
    23	its own adversary. Tracing the verifier under the lane's own tracer would
    24	produce a trace the same verifier judges, so a verifier that wanted to hide a
    25	locked-corpus read would simply not report it — the check would grow, the

    33	could read the locked corpus from inside the gate — is stated, not closed.

   552	fn cell_claims_nothing(cell: &str) -> bool {

   556	    // verdict past the whole-cell check below (review of `a5c27fc`).
   557	    let annotated = (cell.starts_with("NOT_RUN ") || cell.starts_with("QUARANTINED"))

   559	            .split(|ch: char| !ch.is_ascii_alphabetic())
   560	            .any(|word| VERDICT_VOCABULARY.contains(&word.to_ascii_lowercase().as_str()));

   562	        || cell == "NOT_RUN"
   563	        || annotated
   564	        || cell.chars().all(|ch| ch == '-' || ch == ':')

   569	fn normalized_markdown_cell(cell: &str) -> String {
   570	    let mut value = cell.trim();
   571	    loop {
   572	        let next = value
   573	            .strip_prefix('`')
   574	            .and_then(|inner| inner.strip_suffix('`'))
   575	            .or_else(|| {
   576	                value
   577	                    .strip_prefix("**")
   578	                    .and_then(|inner| inner.strip_suffix("**"))
   579	            })
   580	            .or_else(|| {
   581	                value
   582	                    .strip_prefix("__")
   583	                    .and_then(|inner| inner.strip_suffix("__"))
   584	            })
   585	            .or_else(|| {
   586	                value
   587	                    .strip_prefix('*')
   588	                    .and_then(|inner| inner.strip_suffix('*'))
   589	            })
   590	            .or_else(|| {
   591	                value
   592	                    .strip_prefix('_')
   593	                    .and_then(|inner| inner.strip_suffix('_'))
   594	            });
   595	        match next {
   596	            Some(inner) => value = inner.trim(),
   597	            None => break,
   598	        }
   599	    }
   600	    value.to_ascii_lowercase()

   603	/// The rows of the table whose header starts with `header`, each split into
   604	/// trimmed cells. The separator row is dropped.
   605	/// Every table under `header`, with the width its own header line declares.
   606	/// Blind pass 1 at `6b36bbb9` (A03): this found the FIRST header and stopped,
   607	/// so a second table spelling the same header was never read — its rows could
   608	/// claim anything. A document may render a header more than once, so all of
   609	/// them are returned and each is judged against its own header's width.
   610	fn markdown_tables<'a>(text: &'a str, header: &str) -> Vec<(usize, Vec<Vec<&'a str>>)> {
   611	    let mut tables = Vec::new();
   612	    for (offset, _) in text.match_indices(header) {
   613	        let is_line_start = text[..offset]
   614	            .chars()
   615	            .next_back()
   616	            .is_none_or(|previous| previous == '\n');
   617	        if !is_line_start {
   618	            continue;
   619	        }
   620	        let mut lines = text[offset..].lines();
   621	        let width = lines
   622	            .next()
   623	            .map(|line| line.trim().trim_matches('|').split('|').count())
   624	            .unwrap_or_default();
   625	        let mut rows = Vec::new();
   626	        for line in lines {
   627	            if !line.starts_with('|') {
   628	                break;
   629	            }
   630	            let cells = line
   631	                .trim_matches('|')
   632	                .split('|')
   633	                .map(str::trim)
   634	                .collect::<Vec<_>>();
   635	            if cells
   636	                .iter()
   637	                .all(|cell| cell.chars().all(|ch| ch == '-' || ch == ':'))
   638	            {
   639	                continue;
   640	            }
   641	            rows.push(cells);
   642	        }
   643	        tables.push((width, rows));
   644	    }
   645	    tables
   646	}

  1719	/// Independent source/CST oracle. It compares raw observed bytes, not parser
  1720	/// equality or a formatter-owned snapshot.
  1721	/// The coarse scan judged against the source directly, never against the fine
  1722	/// parse: presence, ranges, classification and the hash relation. Returns the
  1723	/// classifications and hashes so the case witness binds them.
  1724	#[allow(clippy::too_many_lines)]
  1725	fn verify_coarse_scan(
  1726	    source: &str,
  1727	    coarse: &liminal_cst::CstDocument,
  1728	) -> Result<(Vec<&'static str>, Vec<String>)> {
  1729	    // The coarse scan is judged against the source directly, never against
  1730	    // the fine parse: a document with a non-blank line has at least one block,
  1731	    // every block's range lies inside the source and holds no blank line, and
  1732	    // the blocks do not overlap (A01).
  1733	    anyhow::ensure!(
  1734	        coarse.source == source,
  1735	        "coarse_parse changed the source it was given"
  1736	    );
  1737	    let has_content = source.lines().any(|line| !line.trim().is_empty());
  1738	    anyhow::ensure!(
  1739	        has_content != coarse.blocks.is_empty(),
  1740	        "coarse_parse found {} blocks for a document that {} content",
  1741	        coarse.blocks.len(),
  1742	        if has_content { "has" } else { "has no" }
  1743	    );
  1744	    // A01: independently reconstruct the blank-line block boundaries. Coverage
  1745	    // alone would let one block span several logical blocks and still pass.
  1746	    let mut expected_ranges = Vec::new();
  1747	    let mut expected_start = None;
  1748	    let mut line_start = 0usize;
  1749	    for line in source.split_inclusive('\n') {
  1750	        let line_end = line_start + line.len();
  1751	        if line.trim().is_empty() {
  1752	            if let Some(start) = expected_start.take() {
  1753	                expected_ranges.push((start, line_start));
  1754	            }
  1755	        } else if expected_start.is_none() {
  1756	            expected_start = Some(line_start);
  1757	        }
  1758	        line_start = line_end;
  1759	    }
  1760	    if let Some(start) = expected_start {
  1761	        expected_ranges.push((start, source.len()));
  1762	    }
  1763	    anyhow::ensure!(
  1764	        coarse.blocks.len() == expected_ranges.len(),
  1765	        "coarse scan reported {} blocks, expected {} blank-line blocks",
  1766	        coarse.blocks.len(),
  1767	        expected_ranges.len()
  1768	    );
  1769	    for (index, (block, (expected_start, expected_end))) in
  1770	        coarse.blocks.iter().zip(expected_ranges).enumerate()
  1771	    {
  1772	        let actual_start = usize::try_from(block.range.start).unwrap_or(usize::MAX);
  1773	        let actual_end = usize::try_from(block.range.end).unwrap_or(usize::MAX);
  1774	        anyhow::ensure!(
  1775	            (actual_start, actual_end) == (expected_start, expected_end),
  1776	            "coarse block {index} has range {actual_start}..{actual_end}, expected {expected_start}..{expected_end}"
  1777	        );
  1778	    }
  1779	    let mut previous_end = 0usize;
  1780	    let mut kinds = Vec::new();
  1781	    let mut hashes = Vec::new();
  1782	    let mut by_text: BTreeMap<&str, String> = BTreeMap::new();
  1783	    let mut by_hash: BTreeMap<String, &str> = BTreeMap::new();
  1784	    for block in &coarse.blocks {
  1785	        let start = usize::try_from(block.range.start).unwrap_or(usize::MAX);
  1786	        let end = usize::try_from(block.range.end).unwrap_or(usize::MAX);
  1787	        anyhow::ensure!(
  1788	            start < end && end <= source.len() && start >= previous_end,
  1789	            "coarse block {start}..{end} is empty, out of range, or overlaps its predecessor"
  1790	        );
  1791	        anyhow::ensure!(
  1792	            source
  1793	                .get(start..end)
  1794	                .is_some_and(|text| text.lines().any(|line| !line.trim().is_empty())),
  1795	            "coarse block {start}..{end} holds no content"
  1796	        );
  1797	        // Blind pass 1 at c29bc0ea (A01): the scan's ranges were judged and
  1798	        // its classification was not, so `coarse_parse` could label every
  1799	        // block alike and no generated case would notice. The kind is
  1800	        // re-derived from the block's own first line, never read back from
  1801	        // the production classifier ADR-0020 §5 forbids this oracle to reach.
  1802	        // What this catches is the classifier drifting from its rule — a
  1803	        // mutation, a reordered branch, a dropped case. It cannot catch the
  1804	        // rule itself being wrong, because the rule is what it restates.
  1805	        let text = source.get(start..end).unwrap_or_default();
  1806	        let first = text.lines().next().unwrap_or_default().trim_start();
  1807	        let hash_marks = first.chars().take_while(|ch| *ch == '#').count();
  1808	        let expected = if first.starts_with("```") {
  1809	            "fence"
  1810	        } else if hash_marks > 0 && first[hash_marks..].starts_with(' ') {
  1811	            "heading"
  1812	        } else if first.starts_with("- ") || first.starts_with("* ") {
  1813	            "list"
  1814	        } else if first.starts_with('@') {
  1815	            "directive"
  1816	        } else if first.starts_with("![") || first.contains("](") {
  1817	            "resource-reference"
  1818	        } else {
  1819	            "paragraph-like"
  1820	        };
  1821	        // `DocumentRoot`, `EmbeddedLanguage` and `Unknown` are declared by the
  1822	        // enum and produced by nothing the coarse scan does. If one appears,
  1823	        // the scan has grown a rule this oracle was never given, and saying so
  1824	        // is more use than a mismatch that reads like a misclassification.
  1825	        let actual = match block.coarse_kind {
  1826	            liminal_cst::CoarseKind::Fence => "fence",
  1827	            liminal_cst::CoarseKind::Heading => "heading",
  1828	            liminal_cst::CoarseKind::List => "list",
  1829	            liminal_cst::CoarseKind::Directive => "directive",
  1830	            liminal_cst::CoarseKind::ResourceReference => "resource-reference",
  1831	            liminal_cst::CoarseKind::ParagraphLike => "paragraph-like",
  1832	            other => anyhow::bail!(
  1833	                "coarse block {start}..{end} is classified {other:?}, a kind the coarse scan \
  1834	                 did not emit when this oracle was written: {text:?}"
  1835	            ),
  1836	        };
  1837	        anyhow::ensure!(
  1838	            actual == expected,
  1839	            "coarse block {start}..{end} is classified {actual}, not {expected}: {text:?}"
  1840	        );
  1841	        // Blind pass 1 at ee646f8c (A01): ranges and kinds were judged and the
  1842	        // block hash was not, so a hash that ignored its bytes went unseen.
  1843	        // Checked as a relation rather than a value: equal text hashes alike,
  1844	        // different text does not. That catches a constant or text-blind hash
  1845	        // without this oracle restating the digest production computes.
  1846	        // `to_hex`, not `{:?}`: the witness is a durable digest, and keying it
  1847	        // on a Debug impl would move it if that impl were ever reformatted
  1848	        // (review of 98f65011).
  1849	        let digest = block.hash.to_hex();
  1850	        if let Some(seen) = by_text.insert(text, digest.clone()) {
  1851	            anyhow::ensure!(
  1852	                seen == digest,
  1853	                "coarse blocks with identical text hash differently: {text:?}"
  1854	            );
  1855	        }
  1856	        if let Some(seen) = by_hash.insert(digest.clone(), text) {
  1857	            anyhow::ensure!(
  1858	                seen == text,
  1859	                "coarse blocks with different text share hash {digest}: {seen:?} and {text:?}"
  1860	            );
  1861	        }
  1862	        kinds.push(actual);
  1863	        hashes.push(digest);
  1864	        previous_end = end;
  1865	    }
  1866	    Ok((kinds, hashes))
  1867	}

  1869	/// Characters the dialect lowers into structure: lists, headings, quotes,
  1870	/// tables and fences. Losing one of these to formatting is the formatter
  1871	/// working; losing anything else that is not whitespace is losing content.
  1872	const STRUCTURAL_MARKUP: [char; 7] = ['-', '*', '#', '>', '|', '+', '`'];
  1873	
  1874	/// A document's words in order. An escape stands for the character it
  1875	/// denotes, so `\n` inside an emitted literal is a separator and not the
  1876	/// letter `n` glued to the next word — without that, escaping a newline
  1877	/// looks like reordering.
  1878	///
  1879	/// Review of `ec045588`: an escape the emitter does not produce — `\u` with
  1880	/// too few hex digits, say — is normalised imperfectly, and that is safe
  1881	/// because this runs over BOTH sides. Mangling can only add words to the
  1882	/// output, never remove one from the source, and added words are what a
  1883	/// subsequence tolerates. Every character the emitter actually escapes is
  1884	/// non-alphanumeric, so it already separates words in the source.
  1885	fn sequence(text: &str) -> Vec<String> {
  1886	    let mut plain = String::with_capacity(text.len());
  1887	    let mut chars = text.chars().peekable();
  1888	    while let Some(ch) = chars.next() {
  1889	        if ch != '\\' {
  1890	            plain.push(ch);
  1891	            continue;
  1892	        }
  1893	        // `\uXXXX` and `\xNN` denote one character each; anything else
  1894	        // after a backslash denotes the character that follows it.
  1895	        let digits = match chars.peek() {
  1896	            Some('u') => 4,
  1897	            Some('x') => 2,
  1898	            _ => 0,
  1899	        };
  1900	        chars.next();
  1901	        for _ in 0..digits {
  1902	            if chars.peek().is_some_and(char::is_ascii_hexdigit) {
  1903	                chars.next();
  1904	            }
  1905	        }
  1906	        plain.push(' ');
  1907	    }
  1908	    plain
  1909	        .split(|ch: char| !ch.is_alphanumeric())
  1910	        .filter(|run| !run.is_empty())
  1911	        .map(str::to_owned)
  1912	        .collect()
  1913	}

  1915	fn independent_oracle_source_cst(
  1916	    source: &str,
  1917	    emitted: &str,
  1918	    once: &str,
  1919	    twice: &str,
  1920	    content: &str,
  1921	    coarse: &liminal_cst::CstDocument,
  1922	) -> Result<Vec<u8>> {
  1923	    anyhow::ensure!(emitted == source, "CST emit is not lossless for {source:?}");
  1924	    anyhow::ensure!(once == twice, "formatting is not idempotent");
  1925	    // Blind pass 1 at 5fb1b57 (A01): those two say nothing about whether
  1926	    // formatting KEPT the document. A formatter returning a constant is
  1927	    // idempotent, and the lossless check never touches the formatter at all.
  1928	    // The generated word is content, not layout: formatting may move it, never
  1929	    // lose it. A durable-marker set would be the natural check and is nearly
  1930	    // vacuous for this corpus, where only the malformed categories carry `{#`.
  1931	    // Alphanumeric runs, not the raw token: a generated word can begin with
  1932	    // markdown syntax (`- v`), and lowering `- ` into list structure is the
  1933	    // formatter doing its job, not losing content.
  1934	    // Blind pass 1 at 91b54842 (A01): the runs were filtered to three
  1935	    // characters and up. `Rng::word` draws one to twelve characters from an
  1936	    // alphabet holding `-`, `_` and a space, so `a`, `x y` and `a-b` are all
  1937	    // reachable tokens with no run that long — for those the survival check
  1938	    // had nothing to check and a formatter could drop the content outright.
  1939	    // Every non-empty run counts now. The dialect numbers nothing (an ordered
  1940	    // block is the keyword `ordered`, never `1.`), so no digit legitimately
  1941	    // disappears, and a one-character run is weak rather than false: it fires
  1942	    // only when that character is absent from the whole output.
  1943	    let words = |text: &str| {
  1944	        text.split(|ch: char| !ch.is_alphanumeric())
  1945	            .filter(|run| !run.is_empty())
  1946	            .map(str::to_owned)
  1947	            .collect::<BTreeSet<_>>()
  1948	    };
  1949	    let lost = words(content)
  1950	        .into_iter()
  1951	        .filter(|word| source.contains(word.as_str()) && !once.contains(word.as_str()))
  1952	        .collect::<Vec<_>>();
  1953	    // Blind pass 1 at `6b36bbb9` (A09): survival was judged on alphanumeric
  1954	    // runs, so content that is punctuation raised nothing — a token of `_`
  1955	    // has no run at all and could be dropped in silence. A character is
  1956	    // markup only if the dialect lowers it: `-`, `*`, `#`, `>`, `|`, `+` and
  1957	    // a backtick begin lists, headings, quotes, tables and fences, and
  1958	    // lowering those is the formatter doing its job. Everything else that is
  1959	    // not whitespace is content and must come back.
  1960	    let lost_marks = content
  1961	        .chars()
  1962	        .filter(|ch| {
  1963	            !ch.is_whitespace()
  1964	                && !ch.is_alphanumeric()
  1965	                && !STRUCTURAL_MARKUP.contains(ch)
  1966	                && source.contains(*ch)
  1967	                && !once.contains(*ch)
  1968	        })
  1969	        .collect::<BTreeSet<_>>();
  1970	    anyhow::ensure!(
  1971	        lost_marks.is_empty(),
  1972	        "formatting dropped the document's punctuation content {lost_marks:?}: {source:?} -> \
  1973	         {once:?}"
  1974	    );
  1975	    anyhow::ensure!(
  1976	        lost.is_empty(),
  1977	        "formatting dropped the document's content {lost:?}: {source:?} -> {once:?}"
  1978	    );
  1979	    // Blind pass 1 at `0a0b4b4b` (A01): membership was checked and ORDER was
  1980	    // not, so a formatter that scrambled a document's words kept every word,
  1981	    // every mark, non-emptiness and idempotence, and lost the meaning. A
  1982	    // formatter may move a word between lines; it may never move one past
  1983	    // another, so the sequence of alphanumeric runs is invariant.
  1984	    // Formatting may ADD words — the explicit dialect wraps content in `node`,
  1985	    // `paragraph`, `literal` — so the source's words must appear in the output
  1986	    // in their own order, not as the whole of it.
  1987	    let emitted_words = sequence(once);
  1988	    let source_words = sequence(source);
  1989	    let mut next = emitted_words.iter();
  1990	    if !source_words
  1991	        .iter()
  1992	        .all(|word| next.any(|candidate| candidate == word))
  1993	    {
  1994	        // Review of `ec045588`: a subsequence fails for two different reasons
  1995	        // and they are not the same defect. If some word appears fewer times
  1996	        // in the output than in the source, the formatter dropped a copy —
  1997	        // which the loss check above cannot see, because it asks whether the
  1998	        // word survives at all and not how often. Otherwise every word is
  1999	        // present the right number of times and the order changed.
  2000	        let count = |words: &[String], word: &String| words.iter().filter(|w| *w == word).count();
  2001	        let dropped = source_words
  2002	            .iter()
  2003	            .find(|word| count(&source_words, word) > count(&emitted_words, word));
  2004	        anyhow::ensure!(
  2005	            dropped.is_none(),
  2006	            "formatting dropped a copy of {:?}: {source:?} -> {once:?}",
  2007	            dropped.expect("checked")
  2008	        );
  2009	        anyhow::bail!("formatting reordered the document's words: {source:?} -> {once:?}");
  2010	    }
  2011	    anyhow::ensure!(
  2012	        source.trim().is_empty() || !once.trim().is_empty(),
  2013	        "formatting emptied a non-empty document"
  2014	    );
  2015	    let (kinds, hashes) = verify_coarse_scan(source, coarse)?;
  2016	    // Blind pass 1 at `cbed339f` (A01): lowering a marker is the formatter's
  2017	    // job, and dropping one is not, and nothing told the two apart. `- alpha`
  2018	    // formatted to a bare `alpha` kept every word and lost the list. Every
  2019	    // block the scan classifies as structure must come back as the explicit
  2020	    // node the dialect lowers it to, or verbatim, as a region the formatter
  2021	    // preserved rather than canonicalized (D20.6).
  2022	    for block in &coarse.blocks {
  2023	        let node = match block.coarse_kind {
  2024	            liminal_cst::CoarseKind::List => "node unordered-list",
  2025	            liminal_cst::CoarseKind::Heading => "node heading",
  2026	            liminal_cst::CoarseKind::Fence => "node code-block",
  2027	            _ => continue,
  2028	        };
  2029	        let range = usize::try_from(block.range.start)?..usize::try_from(block.range.end)?;
  2030	        let first = source
  2031	            .get(range)
  2032	            .context("the coarse scan's block lies inside its source")?
  2033	            .lines()
  2034	            .next()
  2035	            .unwrap_or_default()
  2036	            .trim();
  2037	        anyhow::ensure!(
  2038	            once.contains(node) || once.contains(first),
  2039	            "formatting dropped the structure of {:?} block {first:?}: neither {node:?} nor \
  2040	             the block itself survives: {source:?} -> {once:?}",
  2041	            block.coarse_kind
  2042	        );
  2043	    }
  2044	    let mut witness = emitted.as_bytes().to_vec();
  2045	    witness.extend_from_slice(once.as_bytes());
  2046	    witness.extend_from_slice(format!("coarse:{}", coarse.blocks.len()).as_bytes());
  2047	    witness.extend_from_slice(kinds.join(",").as_bytes());
  2048	    witness.extend_from_slice(hashes.join(",").as_bytes());
  2049	    Ok(witness)
  2050	}

  2052	/// Independent merge oracle. It checks raw content and outcome classes, not
  2053	/// merge-result equality.
  2054	fn independent_oracle_source_transform(
  2055	    base: &str,
  2056	    ours: &str,
  2057	    theirs: &str,
  2058	    identity: &liminal_source::merge::MergeOutcome,
  2059	    forward: &liminal_source::merge::MergeOutcome,
  2060	    swapped: &liminal_source::merge::MergeOutcome,
  2061	) -> Result<Vec<u8>> {
  2062	    let liminal_source::merge::MergeOutcome::Disjoint { merged } = identity else {
  2063	        anyhow::bail!("identity merge reported non-disjoint outcome: {identity:?}");
  2064	    };
  2065	    let merged_tokens = merged.split_whitespace().collect::<Vec<_>>();
  2066	    let ours_tokens = ours.split_whitespace().collect::<Vec<_>>();
  2067	    let mut merged_multiset = merged_tokens.clone();
  2068	    let mut ours_multiset = ours_tokens.clone();
  2069	    merged_multiset.sort_unstable();
  2070	    ours_multiset.sort_unstable();
  2071	    anyhow::ensure!(
  2072	        ours_multiset == merged_multiset,
  2073	        "identity merge dropped content: {ours:?} -> {merged:?}"
  2074	    );
  2075	    // Token multisets alone permit an implementation to drop or duplicate
  2076	    // durable markers. The merge contract keeps base slot order as its primary
  2077	    // layout; a pure move is therefore intentionally not an order-preserving
  2078	    // relation, but its marker set must still survive exactly.
  2079	    let marker_order = |text: &str| {
  2080	        text.split_whitespace()
  2081	            .filter(|token| token.starts_with("{#") && token.ends_with('}'))
  2082	            .map(str::to_owned)
  2083	            .collect::<Vec<_>>()
  2084	    };
  2085	    let base_markers = marker_order(base);
  2086	    let ours_markers = marker_order(ours);
  2087	    if ours_markers != base_markers {
  2088	        let mut expected = ours_markers.clone();
  2089	        let mut actual = marker_order(merged);
  2090	        expected.sort_unstable();
  2091	        actual.sort_unstable();
  2092	        anyhow::ensure!(
  2093	            actual == expected,
  2094	            "identity merge changed durable marker set under layout normalization"
  2095	        );
  2096	        // Blind pass 1 at 612cbcc (A02): the marker SET surviving a move said
  2097	        // nothing about which content each marker kept; swapping the contents
  2098	        // of two moved markers passed. A move keeps every marker's content.
  2099	        let markered = |text: &str| {
  2100	            ordered_block_contents(text)
  2101	                .into_iter()
  2102	                .filter(|(marker, _)| marker.starts_with("{#"))
  2103	                .collect::<BTreeMap<_, _>>()
  2104	        };
  2105	        anyhow::ensure!(
  2106	            markered(merged) == markered(ours),
  2107	            "identity merge re-associated content across moved markers: {ours:?} -> {merged:?}"
  2108	        );
  2109	    }

  2167	fn ordered_block_contents(text: &str) -> BTreeMap<String, Vec<String>> {
  2168	    let mut anonymous = 0usize;
  2169	    let mut blocks = BTreeMap::new();
  2170	    for block in text.split("\n\n") {
  2171	        let marker = block
  2172	            .split_whitespace()
  2173	            .find(|token| token.starts_with("{#") && token.ends_with('}'))
  2174	            .map_or_else(
  2175	                || {
  2176	                    let key = format!("anon:{anonymous}");
  2177	                    anonymous += 1;
  2178	                    key
  2179	                },
  2180	                str::to_owned,
  2181	            );
  2182	        let tokens = block
  2183	            .split_whitespace()
  2184	            .filter(|token| !token.starts_with("{#") || !token.ends_with('}'))
  2185	            .map(str::to_owned)
  2186	            .collect::<Vec<_>>();
  2187	        // Blocks containing only marker tokens carry no ordinary content whose
  2188	        // order can falsify this ordering oracle; marker order is checked above.
  2189	        if !tokens.is_empty() {
  2190	            blocks.insert(marker, tokens);
  2191	        }
  2192	    }
  2193	    blocks
  2194	}

  2196	/// Independent repair oracle. It checks the declared edge set against the
  2197	/// returned order and records that permutation of input edges is stable.
  2198	fn independent_oracle_source_repair(
  2199	    order: &[liminal_id::RepairStepId],
  2200	    ids: &[liminal_id::RepairStepId],
  2201	    edges: &[(usize, usize)],
  2202	    permuted_order: &[liminal_id::RepairStepId],
  2203	) -> Result<Vec<u8>> {
  2204	    let position: BTreeMap<liminal_id::RepairStepId, usize> = order
  2205	        .iter()
  2206	        .enumerate()
  2207	        .map(|(index, id)| (*id, index))
  2208	        .collect();
  2209	    // Blind pass 1 at f360e90 (A03): equal length let a duplicated step stand
  2210	    // in for a missing one. The order is exactly the declared steps, once each.
  2211	    let mut declared = ids.to_vec();
  2212	    let mut returned = order.to_vec();
  2213	    declared.sort_unstable();
  2214	    returned.sort_unstable();
  2215	    anyhow::ensure!(
  2216	        declared == returned && declared.windows(2).all(|pair| pair[0] != pair[1]),
  2217	        "ordering dropped, duplicated or invented steps"
  2218	    );
  2219	    for (before, after) in edges {
  2220	        anyhow::ensure!(
  2221	            position[&ids[*before]] < position[&ids[*after]],
  2222	            "ordering violated a declared dependency"
  2223	        );
  2224	    }
  2225	    anyhow::ensure!(
  2226	        permuted_order == order,
  2227	        "topological order changed under permutation of dependency edges"
  2228	    );
  2229	    Ok(order
  2230	        .iter()
  2231	        .flat_map(|id| id.as_uuid().into_bytes())
  2232	        .collect())
  2233	}

  2235	/// Independent invalidation oracle. It compares expected read membership to
  2236	/// observed invalidation answers, including a negative witness.
  2237	fn independent_oracle_source_invalidation(
  2238	    deps: &mut liminal_revision::ComponentDeps,
  2239	    expected: &BTreeSet<liminal_id::JurisdictionKey>,
  2240	    unrelated: &liminal_id::JurisdictionKey,
  2241	    extra: &liminal_id::JurisdictionKey,
  2242	) -> Result<Vec<u8>> {
  2243	    for key in expected {
  2244	        anyhow::ensure!(
  2245	            deps.invalidated_by(key),
  2246	            "a recorded read did not invalidate: {key:?}"
  2247	        );
  2248	    }
  2249	    anyhow::ensure!(
  2250	        !deps.invalidated_by(unrelated),
  2251	        "an unread key invalidated the computation: {unrelated:?}"
  2252	    );
  2253	    // Add a new dependency only between observations. This makes the second
  2254	    // check a real monotonicity assertion instead of repeating the first one.
  2255	    anyhow::ensure!(
  2256	        !deps.invalidated_by(extra),
  2257	        "extra dependency was already present before monotonicity probe: {extra:?}"
  2258	    );
  2259	    deps.record(extra.clone());
  2260	    // Blind pass 1 at aa00d41 (A03): the relation only re-checked the keys that
  2261	    // already invalidated, so a `record` that did nothing passed. Monotonicity
  2262	    // is that the new read is now observed AND no old one was lost.
  2263	    anyhow::ensure!(
  2264	        deps.invalidated_by(extra),
  2265	        "recording a read did not make it invalidate: {extra:?}"
  2266	    );
  2267	    for key in expected {
  2268	        anyhow::ensure!(
  2269	            deps.invalidated_by(key),
  2270	            "recording another read un-invalidated {key:?}"
  2271	        );
  2272	    }
  2273	    anyhow::ensure!(
  2274	        !deps.invalidated_by(unrelated),
  2275	        "recording a read invalidated an unread key: {unrelated:?}"
  2276	    );
  2277	    let mut witness = Vec::new();
  2278	    for key in expected.iter().chain([unrelated, extra]) {
  2279	        witness.push(u8::from(deps.invalidated_by(key)));
  2280	    }
  2281	    Ok(witness)
  2282	}

  1723	/// classifications and hashes so the case witness binds them.

  1727	    coarse: &liminal_cst::CstDocument,

  1732	    // the blocks do not overlap (A01).

  1739	        has_content != coarse.blocks.is_empty(),
  1740	        "coarse_parse found {} blocks for a document that {} content",
  1741	        coarse.blocks.len(),

  1745	    // alone would let one block span several logical blocks and still pass.

  1761	        expected_ranges.push((start, source.len()));

  1764	        coarse.blocks.len() == expected_ranges.len(),
  1765	        "coarse scan reported {} blocks, expected {} blank-line blocks",
  1766	        coarse.blocks.len(),
  1767	        expected_ranges.len()
  1768	    );

  1770	        coarse.blocks.iter().zip(expected_ranges).enumerate()
  1771	    {
  1772	        let actual_start = usize::try_from(block.range.start).unwrap_or(usize::MAX);
  1773	        let actual_end = usize::try_from(block.range.end).unwrap_or(usize::MAX);

  1788	            start < end && end <= source.len() && start >= previous_end,

  1812	        } else if first.starts_with("- ") || first.starts_with("* ") {

  1814	        } else if first.starts_with('@') {

  1827	            liminal_cst::CoarseKind::Heading => "heading",
  1828	            liminal_cst::CoarseKind::List => "list",
  1829	            liminal_cst::CoarseKind::Directive => "directive",
  1830	            liminal_cst::CoarseKind::ResourceReference => "resource-reference",

  1836	        };
  1837	        anyhow::ensure!(
  1838	            actual == expected,
  1839	            "coarse block {start}..{end} is classified {actual}, not {expected}: {text:?}"
  1840	        );
  1841	        // Blind pass 1 at ee646f8c (A01): ranges and kinds were judged and the
  1842	        // block hash was not, so a hash that ignored its bytes went unseen.

  1852	                seen == digest,
  1853	                "coarse blocks with identical text hash differently: {text:?}"
  1854	            );
  1855	        }

  1857	            anyhow::ensure!(
  1858	                seen == text,
  1859	                "coarse blocks with different text share hash {digest}: {seen:?} and {text:?}"
  1860	            );
  1861	        }
  1862	        kinds.push(actual);
  1863	        hashes.push(digest);
  1864	        previous_end = end;
  1865	    }
  1866	    Ok((kinds, hashes))

  1869	/// Characters the dialect lowers into structure: lists, headings, quotes,
  1870	/// tables and fences. Losing one of these to formatting is the formatter
  1871	/// working; losing anything else that is not whitespace is losing content.
  1872	const STRUCTURAL_MARKUP: [char; 7] = ['-', '*', '#', '>', '|', '+', '`'];

  1874	/// A document's words in order. An escape stands for the character it
  1875	/// denotes, so `\n` inside an emitted literal is a separator and not the
  1876	/// letter `n` glued to the next word — without that, escaping a newline
  1877	/// looks like reordering.
  1878	///
  1879	/// Review of `ec045588`: an escape the emitter does not produce — `\u` with
  1880	/// too few hex digits, say — is normalised imperfectly, and that is safe
  1881	/// because this runs over BOTH sides. Mangling can only add words to the
  1882	/// output, never remove one from the source, and added words are what a
  1883	/// subsequence tolerates. Every character the emitter actually escapes is
  1884	/// non-alphanumeric, so it already separates words in the source.
  1885	fn sequence(text: &str) -> Vec<String> {
  1886	    let mut plain = String::with_capacity(text.len());
  1887	    let mut chars = text.chars().peekable();
  1888	    while let Some(ch) = chars.next() {
  1889	        if ch != '\\' {
  1890	            plain.push(ch);
  1891	            continue;
  1892	        }
  1893	        // `\uXXXX` and `\xNN` denote one character each; anything else
  1894	        // after a backslash denotes the character that follows it.
  1895	        let digits = match chars.peek() {
  1896	            Some('u') => 4,
  1897	            Some('x') => 2,
  1898	            _ => 0,
  1899	        };
  1900	        chars.next();
  1901	        for _ in 0..digits {
  1902	            if chars.peek().is_some_and(char::is_ascii_hexdigit) {
  1903	                chars.next();
  1904	            }
  1905	        }
  1906	        plain.push(' ');
  1907	    }
  1908	    plain
  1909	        .split(|ch: char| !ch.is_alphanumeric())
  1910	        .filter(|run| !run.is_empty())
  1911	        .map(str::to_owned)
  1912	        .collect()
  1913	}

  1915	fn independent_oracle_source_cst(
  1916	    source: &str,
  1917	    emitted: &str,
  1918	    once: &str,
  1919	    twice: &str,
  1920	    content: &str,
  1921	    coarse: &liminal_cst::CstDocument,
  1922	) -> Result<Vec<u8>> {

  1926	    // formatting KEPT the document. A formatter returning a constant is
  1927	    // idempotent, and the lossless check never touches the formatter at all.
  1928	    // The generated word is content, not layout: formatting may move it, never
  1929	    // lose it. A durable-marker set would be the natural check and is nearly
  1930	    // vacuous for this corpus, where only the malformed categories carry `{#`.
  1931	    // Alphanumeric runs, not the raw token: a generated word can begin with
  1932	    // markdown syntax (`- v`), and lowering `- ` into list structure is the
  1933	    // formatter doing its job, not losing content.
  1934	    // Blind pass 1 at 91b54842 (A01): the runs were filtered to three
  1935	    // characters and up. `Rng::word` draws one to twelve characters from an
  1936	    // alphabet holding `-`, `_` and a space, so `a`, `x y` and `a-b` are all
  1937	    // reachable tokens with no run that long — for those the survival check
  1938	    // had nothing to check and a formatter could drop the content outright.
  1939	    // Every non-empty run counts now. The dialect numbers nothing (an ordered
  1940	    // block is the keyword `ordered`, never `1.`), so no digit legitimately
  1941	    // disappears, and a one-character run is weak rather than false: it fires
  1942	    // only when that character is absent from the whole output.
  1943	    let words = |text: &str| {
  1944	        text.split(|ch: char| !ch.is_alphanumeric())
  1945	            .filter(|run| !run.is_empty())
  1946	            .map(str::to_owned)
  1947	            .collect::<BTreeSet<_>>()
  1948	    };
  1949	    let lost = words(content)
  1950	        .into_iter()
  1951	        .filter(|word| source.contains(word.as_str()) && !once.contains(word.as_str()))
  1952	        .collect::<Vec<_>>();
  1953	    // Blind pass 1 at `6b36bbb9` (A09): survival was judged on alphanumeric
  1954	    // runs, so content that is punctuation raised nothing — a token of `_`
  1955	    // has no run at all and could be dropped in silence. A character is
  1956	    // markup only if the dialect lowers it: `-`, `*`, `#`, `>`, `|`, `+` and
  1957	    // a backtick begin lists, headings, quotes, tables and fences, and
  1958	    // lowering those is the formatter doing its job. Everything else that is
  1959	    // not whitespace is content and must come back.
  1960	    let lost_marks = content
  1961	        .chars()
  1962	        .filter(|ch| {
  1963	            !ch.is_whitespace()
  1964	                && !ch.is_alphanumeric()
  1965	                && !STRUCTURAL_MARKUP.contains(ch)
  1966	                && source.contains(*ch)
  1967	                && !once.contains(*ch)
  1968	        })
  1969	        .collect::<BTreeSet<_>>();

  1971	        lost_marks.is_empty(),
  1972	        "formatting dropped the document's punctuation content {lost_marks:?}: {source:?} -> \
  1973	         {once:?}"
  1974	    );
  1975	    anyhow::ensure!(
  1976	        lost.is_empty(),
  1977	        "formatting dropped the document's content {lost:?}: {source:?} -> {once:?}"
  1978	    );
  1979	    // Blind pass 1 at `0a0b4b4b` (A01): membership was checked and ORDER was
  1980	    // not, so a formatter that scrambled a document's words kept every word,
  1981	    // every mark, non-emptiness and idempotence, and lost the meaning. A
  1982	    // formatter may move a word between lines; it may never move one past
  1983	    // another, so the sequence of alphanumeric runs is invariant.
  1984	    // Formatting may ADD words — the explicit dialect wraps content in `node`,

  1986	    // in their own order, not as the whole of it.
  1987	    let emitted_words = sequence(once);
  1988	    let source_words = sequence(source);

  1991	        .iter()
  1992	        .all(|word| next.any(|candidate| candidate == word))
  1993	    {
  1994	        // Review of `ec045588`: a subsequence fails for two different reasons
  1995	        // and they are not the same defect. If some word appears fewer times
  1996	        // in the output than in the source, the formatter dropped a copy —
  1997	        // which the loss check above cannot see, because it asks whether the
  1998	        // word survives at all and not how often. Otherwise every word is
  1999	        // present the right number of times and the order changed.
  2000	        let count = |words: &[String], word: &String| words.iter().filter(|w| *w == word).count();
  2001	        let dropped = source_words
  2002	            .iter()
  2003	            .find(|word| count(&source_words, word) > count(&emitted_words, word));
  2004	        anyhow::ensure!(
  2005	            dropped.is_none(),
  2006	            "formatting dropped a copy of {:?}: {source:?} -> {once:?}",
  2007	            dropped.expect("checked")
  2008	        );
  2009	        anyhow::bail!("formatting reordered the document's words: {source:?} -> {once:?}");
  2010	    }
  2011	    anyhow::ensure!(
  2012	        source.trim().is_empty() || !once.trim().is_empty(),
  2013	        "formatting emptied a non-empty document"
  2014	    );

  2017	    // job, and dropping one is not, and nothing told the two apart. `- alpha`
  2018	    // formatted to a bare `alpha` kept every word and lost the list. Every
  2019	    // block the scan classifies as structure must come back as the explicit
  2020	    // node the dialect lowers it to, or verbatim, as a region the formatter
  2021	    // preserved rather than canonicalized (D20.6).

  2023	        let node = match block.coarse_kind {
  2024	            liminal_cst::CoarseKind::List => "node unordered-list",
  2025	            liminal_cst::CoarseKind::Heading => "node heading",
  2026	            liminal_cst::CoarseKind::Fence => "node code-block",
  2027	            _ => continue,
  2028	        };
  2029	        let range = usize::try_from(block.range.start)?..usize::try_from(block.range.end)?;
  2030	        let first = source
  2031	            .get(range)
  2032	            .context("the coarse scan's block lies inside its source")?
  2033	            .lines()
  2034	            .next()
  2035	            .unwrap_or_default()
  2036	            .trim();
  2037	        anyhow::ensure!(
  2038	            once.contains(node) || once.contains(first),
  2039	            "formatting dropped the structure of {:?} block {first:?}: neither {node:?} nor \
  2040	             the block itself survives: {source:?} -> {once:?}",
  2041	            block.coarse_kind
  2042	        );
  2043	    }
  2044	    let mut witness = emitted.as_bytes().to_vec();
  2045	    witness.extend_from_slice(once.as_bytes());
  2046	    witness.extend_from_slice(format!("coarse:{}", coarse.blocks.len()).as_bytes());
  2047	    witness.extend_from_slice(kinds.join(",").as_bytes());
  2048	    witness.extend_from_slice(hashes.join(",").as_bytes());
  2049	    Ok(witness)
  2050	}

  2052	/// Independent merge oracle. It checks raw content and outcome classes, not
  2053	/// merge-result equality.
  2054	fn independent_oracle_source_transform(
  2055	    base: &str,
  2056	    ours: &str,
  2057	    theirs: &str,
  2058	    identity: &liminal_source::merge::MergeOutcome,

  2060	    swapped: &liminal_source::merge::MergeOutcome,

  2068	    let mut ours_multiset = ours_tokens.clone();
  2069	    merged_multiset.sort_unstable();
  2070	    ours_multiset.sort_unstable();
  2071	    anyhow::ensure!(
  2072	        ours_multiset == merged_multiset,
  2073	        "identity merge dropped content: {ours:?} -> {merged:?}"
  2074	    );
  2075	    // Token multisets alone permit an implementation to drop or duplicate
  2076	    // durable markers. The merge contract keeps base slot order as its primary
  2077	    // layout; a pure move is therefore intentionally not an order-preserving
  2078	    // relation, but its marker set must still survive exactly.
  2079	    let marker_order = |text: &str| {
  2080	        text.split_whitespace()
  2081	            .filter(|token| token.starts_with("{#") && token.ends_with('}'))
  2082	            .map(str::to_owned)
  2083	            .collect::<Vec<_>>()
  2084	    };
  2085	    let base_markers = marker_order(base);
  2086	    let ours_markers = marker_order(ours);
  2087	    if ours_markers != base_markers {
  2088	        let mut expected = ours_markers.clone();
  2089	        let mut actual = marker_order(merged);
  2090	        expected.sort_unstable();
  2091	        actual.sort_unstable();
  2092	        anyhow::ensure!(
  2093	            actual == expected,
  2094	            "identity merge changed durable marker set under layout normalization"
  2095	        );
  2096	        // Blind pass 1 at 612cbcc (A02): the marker SET surviving a move said
  2097	        // nothing about which content each marker kept; swapping the contents
  2098	        // of two moved markers passed. A move keeps every marker's content.
  2099	        let markered = |text: &str| {
  2100	            ordered_block_contents(text)
  2101	                .into_iter()
  2102	                .filter(|(marker, _)| marker.starts_with("{#"))
  2103	                .collect::<BTreeMap<_, _>>()
  2104	        };
  2105	        anyhow::ensure!(
  2106	            markered(merged) == markered(ours),
  2107	            "identity merge re-associated content across moved markers: {ours:?} -> {merged:?}"
  2108	        );
  2109	    }

  2111	        anyhow::ensure!(
  2112	            marker_order(merged) == ours_markers,
  2113	            "identity merge reordered durable markers"
  2114	        );
  2115	        anyhow::ensure!(
  2116	            ordered_block_contents(merged) == ordered_block_contents(ours),
  2117	            "identity merge reordered ordinary content: {ours:?} -> {merged:?}"
  2118	        );
  2119	    }
  2120	    // A12: outcome-class symmetry alone lets a merge drop one side's edit while
  2121	    // both forward and swapped results remain `Disjoint`. For every token a
  2122	    // side added beyond the base, require the corresponding disjoint result to
  2123	    // retain that multiplicity. This checks content without reusing merge code.
  2124	    let require_additions = |side: &str, merged: &str, label: &str| -> Result<()> {
  2125	        let counts = |text: &str| {
  2126	            text.split_whitespace()
  2127	                .fold(BTreeMap::new(), |mut counts, token| {
  2128	                    *counts.entry(token.to_owned()).or_insert(0usize) += 1;
  2129	                    counts
  2130	                })
  2131	        };
  2132	        let base_counts = counts(base);
  2133	        let side_counts = counts(side);
  2134	        let merged_counts = counts(merged);
  2135	        for (token, side_count) in side_counts {
  2136	            let base_count = base_counts.get(&token).copied().unwrap_or(0);
  2137	            if side_count > base_count {
  2138	                anyhow::ensure!(
  2139	                    merged_counts.get(&token).copied().unwrap_or(0) >= side_count,
  2140	                    "disjoint {label} merge dropped added token {token:?}: {side:?} -> {merged:?}"
  2141	                );
  2142	            }
  2143	        }
  2144	        Ok(())
  2145	    };
  2146	    if let liminal_source::merge::MergeOutcome::Disjoint { merged } = &forward {
  2147	        require_additions(ours, merged, "forward/ours")?;
  2148	        require_additions(theirs, merged, "forward/theirs")?;
  2149	    }

  2161	        disjoint(forward) == disjoint(swapped),
  2162	        "merge disjointness is not symmetric under swapping sides"
  2163	    );

  2167	fn ordered_block_contents(text: &str) -> BTreeMap<String, Vec<String>> {
  2168	    let mut anonymous = 0usize;
  2169	    let mut blocks = BTreeMap::new();
  2170	    for block in text.split("\n\n") {
  2171	        let marker = block
  2172	            .split_whitespace()
  2173	            .find(|token| token.starts_with("{#") && token.ends_with('}'))
  2174	            .map_or_else(
  2175	                || {
  2176	                    let key = format!("anon:{anonymous}");
  2177	                    anonymous += 1;
  2178	                    key
  2179	                },
  2180	                str::to_owned,
  2181	            );
  2182	        let tokens = block
  2183	            .split_whitespace()
  2184	            .filter(|token| !token.starts_with("{#") || !token.ends_with('}'))
  2185	            .map(str::to_owned)
  2186	            .collect::<Vec<_>>();
  2187	        // Blocks containing only marker tokens carry no ordinary content whose
  2188	        // order can falsify this ordering oracle; marker order is checked above.
  2189	        if !tokens.is_empty() {
  2190	            blocks.insert(marker, tokens);
  2191	        }
  2192	    }
  2193	    blocks
  2194	}

  2196	/// Independent repair oracle. It checks the declared edge set against the
  2197	/// returned order and records that permutation of input edges is stable.
  2198	fn independent_oracle_source_repair(
  2199	    order: &[liminal_id::RepairStepId],
  2200	    ids: &[liminal_id::RepairStepId],
  2201	    edges: &[(usize, usize)],
  2202	    permuted_order: &[liminal_id::RepairStepId],
  2203	) -> Result<Vec<u8>> {
  2204	    let position: BTreeMap<liminal_id::RepairStepId, usize> = order
  2205	        .iter()
  2206	        .enumerate()
  2207	        .map(|(index, id)| (*id, index))
  2208	        .collect();
  2209	    // Blind pass 1 at f360e90 (A03): equal length let a duplicated step stand
  2210	    // in for a missing one. The order is exactly the declared steps, once each.
  2211	    let mut declared = ids.to_vec();
  2212	    let mut returned = order.to_vec();
  2213	    declared.sort_unstable();
  2214	    returned.sort_unstable();
  2215	    anyhow::ensure!(
  2216	        declared == returned && declared.windows(2).all(|pair| pair[0] != pair[1]),
  2217	        "ordering dropped, duplicated or invented steps"
  2218	    );
  2219	    for (before, after) in edges {
  2220	        anyhow::ensure!(
  2221	            position[&ids[*before]] < position[&ids[*after]],
  2222	            "ordering violated a declared dependency"
  2223	        );
  2224	    }
  2225	    anyhow::ensure!(
  2226	        permuted_order == order,
  2227	        "topological order changed under permutation of dependency edges"
  2228	    );
  2229	    Ok(order
  2230	        .iter()
  2231	        .flat_map(|id| id.as_uuid().into_bytes())
  2232	        .collect())
  2233	}

  2235	/// Independent invalidation oracle. It compares expected read membership to
  2236	/// observed invalidation answers, including a negative witness.
  2237	fn independent_oracle_source_invalidation(
  2238	    deps: &mut liminal_revision::ComponentDeps,
  2239	    expected: &BTreeSet<liminal_id::JurisdictionKey>,
  2240	    unrelated: &liminal_id::JurisdictionKey,
  2241	    extra: &liminal_id::JurisdictionKey,
  2242	) -> Result<Vec<u8>> {
  2243	    for key in expected {
  2244	        anyhow::ensure!(
  2245	            deps.invalidated_by(key),
  2246	            "a recorded read did not invalidate: {key:?}"
  2247	        );
  2248	    }
  2249	    anyhow::ensure!(
  2250	        !deps.invalidated_by(unrelated),
  2251	        "an unread key invalidated the computation: {unrelated:?}"
  2252	    );
  2253	    // Add a new dependency only between observations. This makes the second
  2254	    // check a real monotonicity assertion instead of repeating the first one.
  2255	    anyhow::ensure!(
  2256	        !deps.invalidated_by(extra),
  2257	        "extra dependency was already present before monotonicity probe: {extra:?}"
  2258	    );
  2259	    deps.record(extra.clone());
  2260	    // Blind pass 1 at aa00d41 (A03): the relation only re-checked the keys that
  2261	    // already invalidated, so a `record` that did nothing passed. Monotonicity
  2262	    // is that the new read is now observed AND no old one was lost.
  2263	    anyhow::ensure!(
  2264	        deps.invalidated_by(extra),
  2265	        "recording a read did not make it invalidate: {extra:?}"
  2266	    );
  2267	    for key in expected {
  2268	        anyhow::ensure!(
  2269	            deps.invalidated_by(key),
  2270	            "recording another read un-invalidated {key:?}"
  2271	        );
  2272	    }
  2273	    anyhow::ensure!(
  2274	        !deps.invalidated_by(unrelated),
  2275	        "recording a read invalidated an unread key: {unrelated:?}"
  2276	    );
  2277	    let mut witness = Vec::new();
  2278	    for key in expected.iter().chain([unrelated, extra]) {
  2279	        witness.push(u8::from(deps.invalidated_by(key)));
  2280	    }
  2281	    Ok(witness)
  2282	}

  3542	/// The commands a resolution receipt may claim, and the gate RUNS the one it
  3543	/// claims (A09/A10 at 9eca4f0).
  3544	///
  3545	/// Before this, a receipt naming any command with a self-authored
  3546	/// `verification_exit_code: 0` was accepted without the command ever being
  3547	/// executed — the resolution asserted its own success. The command is drawn
  3548	/// from a closed registry rather than run as written: executing arbitrary text
  3549	/// out of an evidence file would hand whoever wrote the file this process.
  3550	const RESOLUTION_COMMANDS: [(&str, &[&str]); 4] = [
  3551	    ("just ci", &["just", "ci"]),
  3552	    ("just haq-inventory", &["just", "haq-inventory"]),
  3553	    ("just haq-canaries", &["just", "haq-canaries"]),
  3554	    (
  3555	        "cargo nextest run --workspace --all-features",
  3556	        &["cargo", "nextest", "run", "--workspace", "--all-features"],
  3557	    ),
  3558	];

  3560	/// The registry's commands are the project's own gates, run with the gate's
  3561	/// environment and no timeout: they are what CI runs, so a hang here is a hang
  3562	/// in CI, visible either way (review of `e490671`). The working directory is a
  3563	/// disposable worktree at the commit the receipt names, never the live tree.
  3564	fn verify_resolution_command_ran(
  3565	    root: &Utf8Path,
  3566	    who: &str,
  3567	    evidence_text: &str,
  3568	    commit: &str,
  3569	) -> Result<()> {
  3570	    let claimed = evidence_text
  3571	        .lines()
  3572	        .find_map(|line| line.trim_start().strip_prefix("verification_command:"))
  3573	        .map(str::trim)
  3574	        .unwrap_or_default();
  3575	    let argv = RESOLUTION_COMMANDS
  3576	        .iter()
  3577	        .find(|(name, _)| *name == claimed)
  3578	        .map(|(_, argv)| *argv)
  3579	        .with_context(|| {
  3580	            format!(
  3581	                "{who}: resolution claims verification command {claimed:?}, which is not one the \
  3582	                 gate can run; the registry is closed so a receipt cannot name a command that \
  3583	                 exists only in its own text"
  3584	            )
  3585	        })?;
  3586	    let (program, rest) = argv.split_first().context("registry command is empty")?;
  3587	    // Blind pass 1 at aecb2ec7 (A12): the command ran against the working
  3588	    // tree, so a receipt claiming a finding was resolved at some commit was
  3589	    // answered by whether the command passes at HEAD. Reachability was
  3590	    // checked and the commit then ignored. It runs in a disposable worktree
  3591	    // checked out at the claimed commit now, which is what the receipt says.
  3592	    let scratch = liminal_scratch::ScratchDir::new("haq-resolution-replay")?;
  3593	    let worktree = scratch.path().to_owned();
  3594	    let add = Command::new("git")
  3595	        .current_dir(root)
  3596	        .args(["worktree", "add", "--detach", "--quiet"])
  3597	        .arg(&worktree)
  3598	        .arg(commit)
  3599	        .output()?;
  3600	    anyhow::ensure!(
  3601	        add.status.success(),
  3602	        "{who}: resolution replay worktree add at {commit} failed: {}",
  3603	        String::from_utf8_lossy(&add.stderr).trim()
  3604	    );
  3605	    let mut guard = WorktreeGuard::new(root, &worktree);
  3606	    let status = Command::new(program)
  3607	        .current_dir(&worktree)
  3608	        .args(rest)
  3609	        .status()
  3610	        .with_context(|| format!("{who}: run resolution verification {claimed:?} at {commit}"))?;
  3611	    guard.remove()?;
  3612	    anyhow::ensure!(
  3613	        status.success(),
  3614	        "{who}: resolution claims {claimed:?} exited zero at {commit}; it exited {status}"
  3615	    );
  3616	    Ok(())
  3617	}

  3542	/// The commands a resolution receipt may claim, and the gate RUNS the one it
  3543	/// claims (A09/A10 at 9eca4f0).
  3544	///
  3545	/// Before this, a receipt naming any command with a self-authored
  3546	/// `verification_exit_code: 0` was accepted without the command ever being
  3547	/// executed — the resolution asserted its own success. The command is drawn
  3548	/// from a closed registry rather than run as written: executing arbitrary text
  3549	/// out of an evidence file would hand whoever wrote the file this process.
  3550	const RESOLUTION_COMMANDS: [(&str, &[&str]); 4] = [
  3551	    ("just ci", &["just", "ci"]),
  3552	    ("just haq-inventory", &["just", "haq-inventory"]),
  3553	    ("just haq-canaries", &["just", "haq-canaries"]),
  3554	    (
  3555	        "cargo nextest run --workspace --all-features",
  3556	        &["cargo", "nextest", "run", "--workspace", "--all-features"],
  3557	    ),
  3558	];

  3560	/// The registry's commands are the project's own gates, run with the gate's
  3561	/// environment and no timeout: they are what CI runs, so a hang here is a hang
  3562	/// in CI, visible either way (review of `e490671`). The working directory is a
  3563	/// disposable worktree at the commit the receipt names, never the live tree.
  3564	fn verify_resolution_command_ran(
  3565	    root: &Utf8Path,
  3566	    who: &str,
  3567	    evidence_text: &str,
  3568	    commit: &str,
  3569	) -> Result<()> {
  3570	    let claimed = evidence_text
  3571	        .lines()
  3572	        .find_map(|line| line.trim_start().strip_prefix("verification_command:"))
  3573	        .map(str::trim)
  3574	        .unwrap_or_default();
  3575	    let argv = RESOLUTION_COMMANDS
  3576	        .iter()
  3577	        .find(|(name, _)| *name == claimed)
  3578	        .map(|(_, argv)| *argv)
  3579	        .with_context(|| {
  3580	            format!(
  3581	                "{who}: resolution claims verification command {claimed:?}, which is not one the \
  3582	                 gate can run; the registry is closed so a receipt cannot name a command that \
  3583	                 exists only in its own text"
  3584	            )
  3585	        })?;
  3586	    let (program, rest) = argv.split_first().context("registry command is empty")?;
  3587	    // Blind pass 1 at aecb2ec7 (A12): the command ran against the working
  3588	    // tree, so a receipt claiming a finding was resolved at some commit was
  3589	    // answered by whether the command passes at HEAD. Reachability was
  3590	    // checked and the commit then ignored. It runs in a disposable worktree
  3591	    // checked out at the claimed commit now, which is what the receipt says.
  3592	    let scratch = liminal_scratch::ScratchDir::new("haq-resolution-replay")?;
  3593	    let worktree = scratch.path().to_owned();
  3594	    let add = Command::new("git")
  3595	        .current_dir(root)
  3596	        .args(["worktree", "add", "--detach", "--quiet"])
  3597	        .arg(&worktree)
  3598	        .arg(commit)
  3599	        .output()?;
  3600	    anyhow::ensure!(
  3601	        add.status.success(),
  3602	        "{who}: resolution replay worktree add at {commit} failed: {}",
  3603	        String::from_utf8_lossy(&add.stderr).trim()
  3604	    );
  3605	    let mut guard = WorktreeGuard::new(root, &worktree);
  3606	    let status = Command::new(program)
  3607	        .current_dir(&worktree)
  3608	        .args(rest)
  3609	        .status()
  3610	        .with_context(|| format!("{who}: run resolution verification {claimed:?} at {commit}"))?;
  3611	    guard.remove()?;
  3612	    anyhow::ensure!(
  3613	        status.success(),
  3614	        "{who}: resolution claims {claimed:?} exited zero at {commit}; it exited {status}"
  3615	    );
  3616	    Ok(())
  3617	}

  3552	    ("just haq-inventory", &["just", "haq-inventory"]),
  3553	    ("just haq-canaries", &["just", "haq-canaries"]),

  3560	/// The registry's commands are the project's own gates, run with the gate's
  3561	/// environment and no timeout: they are what CI runs, so a hang here is a hang
  3562	/// in CI, visible either way (review of `e490671`). The working directory is a
  3563	/// disposable worktree at the commit the receipt names, never the live tree.
  3564	fn verify_resolution_command_ran(
  3565	    root: &Utf8Path,
  3566	    who: &str,
  3567	    evidence_text: &str,
  3568	    commit: &str,
  3569	) -> Result<()> {
  3570	    let claimed = evidence_text
  3571	        .lines()
  3572	        .find_map(|line| line.trim_start().strip_prefix("verification_command:"))
  3573	        .map(str::trim)
  3574	        .unwrap_or_default();
  3575	    let argv = RESOLUTION_COMMANDS
  3576	        .iter()
  3577	        .find(|(name, _)| *name == claimed)
  3578	        .map(|(_, argv)| *argv)
  3579	        .with_context(|| {
  3580	            format!(
  3581	                "{who}: resolution claims verification command {claimed:?}, which is not one the \
  3582	                 gate can run; the registry is closed so a receipt cannot name a command that \
  3583	                 exists only in its own text"
  3584	            )

  3590	    // checked and the commit then ignored. It runs in a disposable worktree
  3591	    // checked out at the claimed commit now, which is what the receipt says.
  3592	    let scratch = liminal_scratch::ScratchDir::new("haq-resolution-replay")?;

  3594	    let add = Command::new("git")
  3595	        .current_dir(root)
  3596	        .args(["worktree", "add", "--detach", "--quiet"])
  3597	        .arg(&worktree)
  3598	        .arg(commit)
  3599	        .output()?;
  3600	    anyhow::ensure!(
  3601	        add.status.success(),
  3602	        "{who}: resolution replay worktree add at {commit} failed: {}",
  3603	        String::from_utf8_lossy(&add.stderr).trim()
  3604	    );
  3605	    let mut guard = WorktreeGuard::new(root, &worktree);
  3606	    let status = Command::new(program)
  3607	        .current_dir(&worktree)
  3608	        .args(rest)
  3609	        .status()
  3610	        .with_context(|| format!("{who}: run resolution verification {claimed:?} at {commit}"))?;
  3611	    guard.remove()?;
  3612	    anyhow::ensure!(
  3613	        status.success(),
  3614	        "{who}: resolution claims {claimed:?} exited zero at {commit}; it exited {status}"
  3615	    );
  3616	    Ok(())
  3617	}

  3542	/// The commands a resolution receipt may claim, and the gate RUNS the one it
  3543	/// claims (A09/A10 at 9eca4f0).
  3544	///

  3546	/// `verification_exit_code: 0` was accepted without the command ever being
  3547	/// executed — the resolution asserted its own success. The command is drawn
  3548	/// from a closed registry rather than run as written: executing arbitrary text
  3549	/// out of an evidence file would hand whoever wrote the file this process.
  3550	const RESOLUTION_COMMANDS: [(&str, &[&str]); 4] = [
  3551	    ("just ci", &["just", "ci"]),
  3552	    ("just haq-inventory", &["just", "haq-inventory"]),
  3553	    ("just haq-canaries", &["just", "haq-canaries"]),
  3554	    (
  3555	        "cargo nextest run --workspace --all-features",

  3560	/// The registry's commands are the project's own gates, run with the gate's
  3561	/// environment and no timeout: they are what CI runs, so a hang here is a hang
  3562	/// in CI, visible either way (review of `e490671`). The working directory is a
  3563	/// disposable worktree at the commit the receipt names, never the live tree.
  3564	fn verify_resolution_command_ran(
  3565	    root: &Utf8Path,
  3566	    who: &str,
  3567	    evidence_text: &str,
  3568	    commit: &str,
  3569	) -> Result<()> {
  3570	    let claimed = evidence_text
  3571	        .lines()
  3572	        .find_map(|line| line.trim_start().strip_prefix("verification_command:"))
  3573	        .map(str::trim)
  3574	        .unwrap_or_default();
  3575	    let argv = RESOLUTION_COMMANDS
  3576	        .iter()
  3577	        .find(|(name, _)| *name == claimed)
  3578	        .map(|(_, argv)| *argv)
  3579	        .with_context(|| {
  3580	            format!(
  3581	                "{who}: resolution claims verification command {claimed:?}, which is not one the \
  3582	                 gate can run; the registry is closed so a receipt cannot name a command that \
  3583	                 exists only in its own text"
  3584	            )
  3585	        })?;
  3586	    let (program, rest) = argv.split_first().context("registry command is empty")?;
  3587	    // Blind pass 1 at aecb2ec7 (A12): the command ran against the working
  3588	    // tree, so a receipt claiming a finding was resolved at some commit was
  3589	    // answered by whether the command passes at HEAD. Reachability was
  3590	    // checked and the commit then ignored. It runs in a disposable worktree
  3591	    // checked out at the claimed commit now, which is what the receipt says.
  3592	    let scratch = liminal_scratch::ScratchDir::new("haq-resolution-replay")?;
  3593	    let worktree = scratch.path().to_owned();
  3594	    let add = Command::new("git")
  3595	        .current_dir(root)
  3596	        .args(["worktree", "add", "--detach", "--quiet"])
  3597	        .arg(&worktree)
  3598	        .arg(commit)
  3599	        .output()?;
  3600	    anyhow::ensure!(
  3601	        add.status.success(),
  3602	        "{who}: resolution replay worktree add at {commit} failed: {}",
  3603	        String::from_utf8_lossy(&add.stderr).trim()
  3604	    );
  3605	    let mut guard = WorktreeGuard::new(root, &worktree);
  3606	    let status = Command::new(program)
  3607	        .current_dir(&worktree)
  3608	        .args(rest)
  3609	        .status()
  3610	        .with_context(|| format!("{who}: run resolution verification {claimed:?} at {commit}"))?;
  3611	    guard.remove()?;
  3612	    anyhow::ensure!(
  3613	        status.success(),
  3614	        "{who}: resolution claims {claimed:?} exited zero at {commit}; it exited {status}"
  3615	    );
  3616	    Ok(())
  3617	}

  4553	        .iter()

  4572	        mutant.requirement,

  4576	        .iter()

  4581	    // is what put one test on 46% of the plan (review of `95a97b8b`).
  4582	    let primary = if observed_candidates.is_empty() {

  4586	    };

  4588	        .iter()
  4589	        .position(|test| test.id == primary.id)

  4593	        .map(after)

  4617	/// changed at or after this commit is the qualifier's own churn rather than
  4618	/// the suite under qualification (AM-17.11).
  4619	const CAMPAIGN_FIRST_LANE: &str = "0d8c32a4ae1afda9808e55c3c291445aad4e3d60";

  4621	/// Whether `coordinate` — a `file:line` a finding names — points at a line

  4623	/// decides whether a finding is fixed or recorded is evidence rather than the
  4624	/// qualifier's judgement about its own work.
  4625	pub fn coordinate_is_campaign_churn(root: &Utf8Path, coordinate: &str) -> Result<bool> {

  4627	        .rsplit_once(':')
  4628	        .with_context(|| format!("{coordinate:?} is not a file:line coordinate"))?;
  4629	    let line: u32 = line
  4630	        .parse()
  4631	        .with_context(|| format!("{coordinate:?} does not name a line"))?;
  4632	    anyhow::ensure!(line > 0, "{coordinate:?} names line zero");
  4633	    let blamed = git_text(
  4634	        root,
  4635	        &[
  4636	            "blame",
  4637	            "--porcelain",
  4638	            "-L",
  4639	            &format!("{line},{line}"),
  4640	            "--",
  4641	            file,
  4642	        ],
  4643	    )
  4644	    .with_context(|| format!("blame {coordinate}"))?;
  4645	    let commit = blamed
  4646	        .split_whitespace()
  4647	        .next()
  4648	        .with_context(|| format!("{coordinate}: blame named no commit"))?;
  4649	    // `merge-base --is-ancestor A B` succeeds when A is an ancestor of B. The
  4650	    // campaign's first lane being an ancestor of the blamed commit means the
  4651	    // line was written during the campaign.
  4652	    let status = Command::new("git")
  4653	        .current_dir(root)
  4654	        .args(["merge-base", "--is-ancestor", CAMPAIGN_FIRST_LANE, commit])
  4655	        .status()
  4656	        .context("git merge-base --is-ancestor")?;

  4658	}

  4660	fn verify_mutant_killing_tests(root: &Utf8Path, packet: &Packet) -> Result<()> {
  4661	    // AM-17.10: the column is derived for every mutant, whatever its
  4662	    // disposition, and is checked before the clauses that inspect only killed
  4663	    // ones. This function used to return here when nothing was killed, so at
  4664	    // stage 1a — where all 65 mutants are predeclared — it read nothing at
  4665	    // all, and a generated killer column rode through fourteen lanes.

  4667	        .mutants
  4668	        .iter()
  4669	        .filter(|mutant| mutant.disposition == "killed")
  4670	        .collect();
  4671	    let by_id: BTreeMap<&str, &Test> = packet
  4672	        .tests
  4673	        .iter()
  4674	        .map(|test| (test.id.as_str(), test))
  4675	        .collect();
  4676	    let ignored = ignored_test_names(root);
  4677	    for mutant in killed {
  4678	        if mutant.killing_tests.is_empty() {
  4679	            anyhow::bail!("{} claims killed but names no killing test", mutant.id);
  4680	        }
  4681	        for test_id in &mutant.killing_tests {
  4682	            let test = by_id.get(test_id.as_str()).with_context(|| {
  4683	                format!(
  4684	                    "{} names killing test {test_id}, which the packet does not declare",
  4685	                    mutant.id

  4690	                anyhow::bail!(
  4691	                    "{} claims killed by {} ({}), which is #[ignore]d — an ignored test \
  4692	                     never runs, so it cannot witness a kill",
  4693	                    mutant.id,
  4694	                    test_id,
  4695	                    test.name
  4696	                );

  4704	    // mutants carried a generated killer column through fourteen lanes with

  4706	    for mutant in &packet.mutants {

  4709	            mutant.killing_tests == derived,
  4710	            "{} names killing tests {:?}; AM-17.10 derives {:?} from requirement {} and \

  4713	            mutant.killing_tests,
  4714	            derived,
  4715	            mutant.requirement,
  4716	            mutant.operator
  4717	        );
  4718	    }
  4719	    Ok(())
  4720	}

  4541	fn derive_killing_tests(packet: &Packet, mutant: &Mutant) -> Result<Vec<String>> {

  4618	/// the suite under qualification (AM-17.11).

  4627	        .rsplit_once(':')
  4628	        .with_context(|| format!("{coordinate:?} is not a file:line coordinate"))?;

  4630	        .parse()
  4631	        .with_context(|| format!("{coordinate:?} does not name a line"))?;

  4634	        root,
  4635	        &[
  4636	            "blame",
  4637	            "--porcelain",
  4638	            "-L",
  4639	            &format!("{line},{line}"),
  4640	            "--",
  4641	            file,
  4642	        ],
  4643	    )
  4644	    .with_context(|| format!("blame {coordinate}"))?;

  4646	        .split_whitespace()
  4647	        .next()
  4648	        .with_context(|| format!("{coordinate}: blame named no commit"))?;

  4653	        .current_dir(root)

  6278	fn verify_fuzz_rows(recorded: &[FuzzEvidence], present: &BTreeSet<String>) -> Result<()> {

  6280	        .iter()
  6281	        .map(|row| row.target.clone())
  6282	        .collect::<BTreeSet<_>>();

  6284	        anyhow::bail!(
  6285	            "fuzz evidence does not cover the targets in the tree: recorded={declared:?}, \
  6286	             present={present:?}"
  6287	        );
  6288	    }
  6289	    require_unique(
  6290	        recorded.iter().map(|row| row.target.as_str()),
  6291	        "fuzz target",
  6292	    )?;

  6295	    // substantiate were unfalsifiable once the run ended. The digest makes a
  6296	    // later-produced log checkable.

  6298	        if row.log_blake3.len() != 64 || !row.log_blake3.chars().all(|c| c.is_ascii_hexdigit()) {
  6299	            anyhow::bail!(
  6300	                "{}: log_blake3 {:?} is not a 64-hex digest, so its log can never be checked",
  6301	                row.target,
  6302	                row.log_blake3
  6303	            );
  6304	        }
  6305	    }

  6308	    // and the evidence had no way to say whether one ran. An unsanitized
  6309	    // campaign finds crashes it can see and silently misses every
  6310	    // memory-safety defect it cannot.
  6311	    for row in recorded {
  6312	        if !matches!(
  6313	            row.sanitizer.as_str(),
  6314	            "address" | "memory" | "thread" | "leak"
  6315	        ) {
  6316	            anyhow::bail!(
  6317	                "{}: sanitizer {:?} is not a sanitizer ADR-0020 §4 accepts",
  6318	                row.target,
  6319	                row.sanitizer
  6320	            );
  6321	        }
  6322	    }

  6324	    let total_minutes: u64 = recorded.iter().map(|row| row.seconds / 60).sum();

  6326	        anyhow::bail!("recorded fuzz budget {total_minutes} target-minutes is below 150");
  6327	    }
  6328	    for row in recorded {
  6329	        if row.exit_code != 0 {
  6330	            anyhow::bail!(
  6331	                "fuzz target {} exited {} with {} artifact(s) — every crash is a failing \
  6332	                 result (ADR-0020 §4)",
  6333	                row.target,
  6334	                row.exit_code,
  6335	                row.artifacts
  6336	            );
  6337	        }
  6338	        if row.artifacts != 0 {
  6339	            anyhow::bail!(
  6340	                "fuzz target {} left {} artifacts",
  6341	                row.target,
  6342	                row.artifacts
  6343	            );
  6344	        }

  6346	            anyhow::bail!("fuzz target {} recorded zero executions", row.target);
  6347	        }

  6349	            anyhow::bail!("fuzz target {} records no log path", row.target);
  6350	        }

  6352	        // sanitizer-enabled fuzz campaign". That is a per-target floor, not just
  6353	        // a contribution to the 150 target-minute total — without it one long
  6354	        // target could carry the sum while another ran for seconds.

  6361	                row.target,
  6362	                row.seconds
  6363	            );
  6364	        }

  6367	        // the evidence should not be able to state.

  6799	fn verify_sanitizer_build_replay(

  6802	    proof: &SanitizerProof,
  6803	    provenance: &Provenance,
  6804	) -> Result<()> {
  6805	    // Rebuild at the CANONICAL path the campaign built at (M17.5 F-42), not a
  6806	    // scratch worktree. Measured: the same commit built at two paths differs in
  6807	    // .rodata by its codegen-unit name, because cargo hashes the fuzz crate's
  6808	    // absolute manifest path into `-C metadata`; two clean builds at one fixed
  6809	    // path are byte-identical. The path and flags are closed here and the proof
  6810	    // must record the same, so neither side can drift from the other.
  6811	    let (build_root, build_rustflags) = sanitizer_build_canon(&provenance.fixed_commit);
  6812	    require_eq(
  6813	        &format!("{} sanitizer build_root", row.target),
  6814	        &proof.build_root,
  6815	        build_root.as_str(),
  6816	    )?;
  6817	    // The cargo-home remap's SOURCE is the campaign machine's $HOME and does
  6818	    // not shape a single byte -- its TARGET (/cargo) does. Comparing the raw
  6819	    // string would refuse a byte-identical build from any machine with a
  6820	    // different home directory (HEAD review). Compare with the source
  6821	    // normalized; the build-root remap and the cwd prefix must still match
  6822	    // exactly, because those DO determine the bytes.
  6823	    require_eq(
  6824	        &format!("{} sanitizer build_rustflags", row.target),
  6825	        &normalize_build_rustflags(&proof.build_rustflags),
  6826	        &normalize_build_rustflags(&build_rustflags),
  6827	    )?;

  6829	    // campaign prunes sibling commits' trees under an exclusive lock, so a
  6830	    // replay mid-build cannot have its worktree removed from under it (HEAD
  6831	    // review). std's File::lock_shared is stable on this toolchain.
  6832	    let base = build_root
  6833	        .parent()
  6834	        .context("canonical build root has a parent")?;
  6835	    fs::create_dir_all(base)?;
  6836	    let lock = fs::File::create(base.join(".lock")).context("open sanitizer build lock")?;
  6837	    lock.lock_shared()
  6838	        .context("shared-lock sanitizer build base")?;

  6841	    // merely when `.git` is. The checkout is `--no-checkout`, then
  6842	    // sparse-checkout, then checkout: interrupt it between those and `.git`
  6843	    // exists over a tree with no `crates/` and a `fuzz/` holding nothing but
  6844	    // the `.cargo` this function writes. Being an existence check on the wrong
  6845	    // file, the old condition then reused that forever, and every run failed

  6847	    // what a `just ci` killed mid-run left behind on 2026-09-20.

  6850	    // opens first, so if it is present the build can start, and if it is not

  6852	    let usable = worktree.join(".git").exists() && worktree.join("fuzz/Cargo.toml").exists();

  6856	            // add` refuses a path it still knows about, so drop the
  6857	            // registration with the directory.

  6859	                .current_dir(root)
  6860	                .args(["worktree", "remove", "--force", worktree.as_str()])
  6861	                .status();

  6863	                fs::remove_dir_all(&worktree).with_context(|| format!("clear stale {worktree}"))?;
  6864	            }

  6866	                .current_dir(root)
  6867	                .args(["worktree", "prune"])
  6868	                .status();
  6869	        }

  6871	            fs::create_dir_all(parent)?;
  6872	        }

  6874	            root,
  6875	            &worktree,
  6876	            &provenance.fixed_commit,
  6877	            "sanitizer replay",
  6878	        )?;
  6879	    }
  6880	    fs::create_dir_all(worktree.join("fuzz/.cargo"))?;

  6882	        worktree.join("fuzz/.cargo/config.toml"),
  6883	        "[unstable]\ntrim-paths = true\n\n[profile.release]\ntrim-paths = \"all\"\n",
  6884	    )?;

  6886	        .current_dir(&worktree)
  6887	        .env("RUSTFLAGS", &build_rustflags)
  6888	        // Pin the target directory to the one the lookup below reads. Cargo
  6889	        // takes `build.target-dir` from `$CARGO_HOME/config.toml`, which is
