  6894	        // if this replay had produced it. The value restores cargo-fuzz's own
  6895	        // default, so recorded digests are unaffected.
  6896	        .env("CARGO_TARGET_DIR", worktree.join("fuzz/target"))
  6897	        .args([
  6898	            &format!("+{SANITIZER_TOOLCHAIN}"),
  6899	            "fuzz",
  6900	            "build",
  6901	            "-s",
  6902	            row.sanitizer.as_str(),
  6903	            row.target.as_str(),
  6904	        ])
  6905	        .output()
  6906	        .with_context(|| format!("replay sanitizer build for {}", row.target))?;

  6908	        output.status.success(),
  6909	        "replayed sanitizer build failed for {}: {}",
  6910	        row.target,

  6915	        .find(|path| path.file_name() == Some(row.target.as_str()))
  6916	        .with_context(|| format!("replayed sanitizer build produced no {} binary", row.target))?;

  6919	        &format!("{} replayed sanitizer binary digest", row.target),

  6921	        &digest,
  6922	    )?;

  6926	        probe_text.contains(runtime_name),
  6927	        "replayed binary for {} does not carry the {} runtime ({runtime_name} absent from its help)",
  6928	        row.target,
  6929	        row.sanitizer
  6930	    );
  6931	    Ok(())
  6932	}

  6934	fn find_named_files(root: &Utf8Path, name: &str) -> Result<Vec<Utf8PathBuf>> {
  6935	    let mut found = Vec::new();
  6936	    if !root.exists() {
  6937	        return Ok(found);
  6938	    }
  6939	    for entry in fs::read_dir(root)? {
  6940	        let entry = entry?;
  6941	        let path = Utf8PathBuf::from_path_buf(entry.path()).map_err(|path| {
  6942	            anyhow::anyhow!("non-UTF-8 path while finding {name}: {}", path.display())
  6943	        })?;
  6944	        if entry.file_type()?.is_dir() {
  6945	            found.extend(find_named_files(&path, name)?);
  6946	        } else if path.file_name() == Some(name) {
  6947	            found.push(path);
  6948	        }
  6949	    }
  6950	    Ok(found)
  6951	}

  6978	        .lines()
  6979	        .filter_map(|line| line.strip_prefix("stat::number_of_executed_units:"))
  6980	        .next_back()
  6981	        .and_then(|value| value.trim().parse::<u64>().ok())

  6989	        &format!("{} log execution count", row.target),
  6990	        &stat_execs.to_string(),
  6991	        &row.execs.to_string(),

  6994	        .lines()
  6995	        .filter_map(|line| line.strip_prefix("Done "))
  6996	        .next_back()
  6997	        .with_context(|| format!("{}: retained fuzz log has no Done footer", row.target))?;
  6998	    let done_execs = done
  6999	        .split_whitespace()
  7000	        .next()
  7001	        .and_then(|value| value.parse::<u64>().ok())
  7002	        .with_context(|| format!("{}: malformed Done execution count", row.target))?;

  7004	        .split(" in ")
  7005	        .nth(1)
  7006	        .and_then(|value| value.split_whitespace().next())
  7007	        .and_then(|value| value.parse::<u64>().ok())
  7008	        .with_context(|| format!("{}: malformed Done elapsed seconds", row.target))?;

  6088	                .extension()
  6089	                .is_some_and(|extension| extension.eq_ignore_ascii_case("json"))

  6097	                "{target}: seed {name} declares the valid class and is not well-formed in its \

  6117	    // class to the table enforces it.

  6120	            counts.get(class).copied().unwrap_or(0) > 0,
  6121	            "{target}: committed seed set has no {class} seed; ADR-0020 §4 requires seeds \
  6122	             spanning valid, boundary, truncated, malformed and hostile input (declared by \
  6123	             name: {:?})",

  6125	                .iter()
  6126	                .map(|(c, t)| (*c, *t))
  6127	                .collect::<Vec<_>>()
  6128	        );
  6129	    }

  6227	/// Digest the seed corpus that is actually COMMITTED (M17.5 F-32).
  6228	///
  6229	/// This read the filesystem and called the result "the committed corpus". It is
  6230	/// not: `.gitignore` excludes `fuzz/corpus/`, so the directory holds sixteen
  6231	/// tracked seeds per target plus every input libFuzzer has written there. The
  6232	/// recorded `seed_count` was therefore a property of ONE MACHINE — 18,233 here
  6233	/// — and a fresh clone, holding the sixteen, could never satisfy it. Killing a
  6234	/// campaign turned a green tree red with no code change.
  6235	///
  6236	/// `git ls-files` fixes it in the direction the error message already claimed,
  6237	/// and sixteen tracked seeds per target is exactly ADR-0020 §4's "at least 16
  6238	/// predeclared seeds".
  6239	fn seed_manifest_digest(root: &Utf8Path, seed_dir: &Utf8Path) -> Result<(u64, String)> {
  6240	    let relative = seed_dir
  6241	        .strip_prefix(root)
  6242	        .unwrap_or(seed_dir)
  6243	        .as_str()
  6244	        .to_owned();
  6245	    let listed = git_text(root, &["ls-files", "-z", "--", &relative])?;
  6246	    let mut files = listed
  6247	        .split('\0')
  6248	        .filter(|name| !name.trim().is_empty())
  6249	        .map(|name| root.join(name))
  6250	        .filter(|path| path.is_file())
  6251	        .collect::<Vec<_>>();
  6252	    anyhow::ensure!(
  6253	        !files.is_empty(),
  6254	        "{seed_dir}: no seed is tracked by git; a corpus that lives only on one \
  6255	         machine cannot reproduce a campaign (ADR-0020 §1)"
  6256	    );
  6257	    files.sort();
  6258	    let mut hasher = blake3::Hasher::new();
  6259	    for path in &files {
  6260	        let name = path
  6261	            .file_name()
  6262	            .with_context(|| format!("{path}: seed has no file name"))?;
  6263	        let bytes = fs::read(path).with_context(|| format!("read fuzz seed {path}"))?;
  6264	        let mut seed_hash = Sha256::new();
  6265	        seed_hash.update(bytes);
  6266	        let seed_hash = format!("{:x}", seed_hash.finalize());
  6267	        hasher.update(name.as_bytes());
  6268	        hasher.update(&[0]);
  6269	        hasher.update(seed_hash.as_bytes());
  6270	        hasher.update(&[0]);
  6271	    }
  6272	    Ok((
  6273	        u64::try_from(files.len()).context("fuzz seed count exceeds u64")?,
  6274	        hasher.finalize().to_hex().to_string(),
  6275	    ))
  6276	}

  6278	fn verify_fuzz_rows(recorded: &[FuzzEvidence], present: &BTreeSet<String>) -> Result<()> {
  6279	    let declared = recorded
  6280	        .iter()
  6281	        .map(|row| row.target.clone())
  6282	        .collect::<BTreeSet<_>>();
  6283	    if &declared != present {
  6284	        anyhow::bail!(
  6285	            "fuzz evidence does not cover the targets in the tree: recorded={declared:?}, \
  6286	             present={present:?}"
  6287	        );
  6288	    }
  6289	    require_unique(
  6290	        recorded.iter().map(|row| row.target.as_str()),
  6291	        "fuzz target",
  6292	    )?;
  6293	
  6294	    // M17.5 F-17: `log` names a gitignored path, so the counts it would
  6295	    // substantiate were unfalsifiable once the run ended. The digest makes a
  6296	    // later-produced log checkable.
  6297	    for row in recorded {
  6298	        if row.log_blake3.len() != 64 || !row.log_blake3.chars().all(|c| c.is_ascii_hexdigit()) {
  6299	            anyhow::bail!(
  6300	                "{}: log_blake3 {:?} is not a 64-hex digest, so its log can never be checked",
  6301	                row.target,
  6302	                row.log_blake3
  6303	            );
  6304	        }
  6305	    }
  6306	
  6307	    // M17.5 F-27 / P1-A09: ADR-0020 §4 requires a SANITIZER-ENABLED campaign
  6308	    // and the evidence had no way to say whether one ran. An unsanitized
  6309	    // campaign finds crashes it can see and silently misses every
  6310	    // memory-safety defect it cannot.
  6311	    for row in recorded {
  6312	        if !matches!(
  6313	            row.sanitizer.as_str(),
  6314	            "address" | "memory" | "thread" | "leak"
  6315	        ) {
  6316	            anyhow::bail!(
  6317	                "{}: sanitizer {:?} is not a sanitizer ADR-0020 §4 accepts",
  6318	                row.target,
  6319	                row.sanitizer
  6320	            );
  6321	        }
  6322	    }
  6323	
  6324	    let total_minutes: u64 = recorded.iter().map(|row| row.seconds / 60).sum();
  6325	    if total_minutes < 150 {
  6326	        anyhow::bail!("recorded fuzz budget {total_minutes} target-minutes is below 150");
  6327	    }
  6328	    for row in recorded {
  6329	        if row.exit_code != 0 {
  6330	            anyhow::bail!(
  6331	                "fuzz target {} exited {} with {} artifact(s) — every crash is a failing \
  6332	                 result (ADR-0020 §4)",
  6333	                row.target,
  6334	                row.exit_code,
  6335	                row.artifacts
  6336	            );
  6337	        }
  6338	        if row.artifacts != 0 {
  6339	            anyhow::bail!(
  6340	                "fuzz target {} left {} artifacts",
  6341	                row.target,
  6342	                row.artifacts
  6343	            );
  6344	        }
  6345	        if row.execs == 0 {
  6346	            anyhow::bail!("fuzz target {} recorded zero executions", row.target);
  6347	        }
  6348	        if row.log.trim().is_empty() {
  6349	            anyhow::bail!("fuzz target {} records no log path", row.target);
  6350	        }
  6351	        // ADR-0020 line 90: "each family also receives one 30-minute
  6352	        // sanitizer-enabled fuzz campaign". That is a per-target floor, not just
  6353	        // a contribution to the 150 target-minute total — without it one long
  6354	        // target could carry the sum while another ran for seconds.
  6355	        //
  6356	        // The same 30-minute floor is used by family budget reconciliation.
  6357	        if row.seconds < 30 * 60 {
  6358	            anyhow::bail!(
  6359	                "fuzz target {} was budgeted {}s, below the 30-minute per-target floor \
  6360	                 (ADR-0020)",
  6361	                row.target,
  6362	                row.seconds
  6363	            );
  6364	        }
  6365	        // A clean campaign runs to its budget. Finishing far short of it means
  6366	        // the target stopped early, and a clean early exit is a contradiction
  6367	        // the evidence should not be able to state.
  6368	        if row.elapsed_s + 60 < row.seconds {
  6369	            anyhow::bail!(
  6370	                "fuzz target {} claims a clean {}s campaign but only ran {}s — an early \
  6371	                 exit with exit_code 0 and no artifacts is not a coherent result",
  6372	                row.target,
  6373	                row.seconds,
  6374	                row.elapsed_s
  6375	            );
  6376	        }
  6377	    }
  6378	    // `haqp_fuzz_campaign.sh` drives every target from ONE `SEED`, so the rows
  6379	    // must agree. Checking only for a nonzero seed would let the comment claim
  6380	    // more than the code enforced — rows carrying three different seeds describe
  6381	    // three campaigns, and none of them is the one the packet points at.
  6382	    let seeds = recorded.iter().map(|row| row.seed).collect::<BTreeSet<_>>();
  6383	    match seeds.iter().copied().next() {
  6384	        None => anyhow::bail!("fuzz evidence records no targets at all"),
  6385	        Some(0) => {
  6386	            anyhow::bail!(
  6387	                "fuzz evidence records no campaign seed, so the lane cannot be reproduced"
  6388	            )
  6389	        }
  6390	        Some(_) if seeds.len() > 1 => anyhow::bail!(
  6391	            "fuzz evidence carries {} distinct seeds {seeds:?}; one campaign has one seed, so \
  6392	             these rows describe runs the packet cannot point at",
  6393	            seeds.len()
  6394	        ),
  6395	        Some(_) => {}
  6396	    }
  6397	    Ok(())
  6398	}

  6799	fn verify_sanitizer_build_replay(

  6801	    row: &FuzzEvidence,
  6802	    proof: &SanitizerProof,
  6803	    provenance: &Provenance,
  6804	) -> Result<()> {

  6806	    // scratch worktree. Measured: the same commit built at two paths differs in
  6807	    // .rodata by its codegen-unit name, because cargo hashes the fuzz crate's
  6808	    // absolute manifest path into `-C metadata`; two clean builds at one fixed
  6809	    // path are byte-identical. The path and flags are closed here and the proof
  6810	    // must record the same, so neither side can drift from the other.
  6811	    let (build_root, build_rustflags) = sanitizer_build_canon(&provenance.fixed_commit);
  6812	    require_eq(
  6813	        &format!("{} sanitizer build_root", row.target),
  6814	        &proof.build_root,
  6815	        build_root.as_str(),
  6816	    )?;

  6818	    // not shape a single byte -- its TARGET (/cargo) does. Comparing the raw
  6819	    // string would refuse a byte-identical build from any machine with a
  6820	    // different home directory (HEAD review). Compare with the source
  6821	    // normalized; the build-root remap and the cwd prefix must still match
  6822	    // exactly, because those DO determine the bytes.
  6823	    require_eq(
  6824	        &format!("{} sanitizer build_rustflags", row.target),
  6825	        &normalize_build_rustflags(&proof.build_rustflags),
  6826	        &normalize_build_rustflags(&build_rustflags),
  6827	    )?;

  6829	    // campaign prunes sibling commits' trees under an exclusive lock, so a
  6830	    // replay mid-build cannot have its worktree removed from under it (HEAD
  6831	    // review). std's File::lock_shared is stable on this toolchain.
  6832	    let base = build_root
  6833	        .parent()
  6834	        .context("canonical build root has a parent")?;
  6835	    fs::create_dir_all(base)?;
  6836	    let lock = fs::File::create(base.join(".lock")).context("open sanitizer build lock")?;
  6837	    lock.lock_shared()
  6838	        .context("shared-lock sanitizer build base")?;

  6840	    // A worktree is reusable only when the build's own inputs are THERE, not
  6841	    // merely when `.git` is. The checkout is `--no-checkout`, then
  6842	    // sparse-checkout, then checkout: interrupt it between those and `.git`
  6843	    // exists over a tree with no `crates/` and a `fuzz/` holding nothing but
  6844	    // the `.cargo` this function writes. Being an existence check on the wrong

  6847	    // what a `just ci` killed mid-run left behind on 2026-09-20.
  6848	    //

  6859	                .current_dir(root)
  6860	                .args(["worktree", "remove", "--force", worktree.as_str()])
  6861	                .status();

  6863	                fs::remove_dir_all(&worktree).with_context(|| format!("clear stale {worktree}"))?;

  6866	                .current_dir(root)
  6867	                .args(["worktree", "prune"])
  6868	                .status();
  6869	        }

  6871	            fs::create_dir_all(parent)?;

  6874	            root,
  6875	            &worktree,
  6876	            &provenance.fixed_commit,
  6877	            "sanitizer replay",
  6878	        )?;
  6879	    }

  6882	        worktree.join("fuzz/.cargo/config.toml"),

  6884	    )?;

  6886	        .current_dir(&worktree)
  6887	        .env("RUSTFLAGS", &build_rustflags)

  6889	        // takes `build.target-dir` from `$CARGO_HOME/config.toml`, which is
  6890	        // outside this repository: when that key was added on 2026-09-18 the

  6898	            &format!("+{SANITIZER_TOOLCHAIN}"),
  6899	            "fuzz",
  6900	            "build",
  6901	            "-s",
  6902	            row.sanitizer.as_str(),

  6915	        .find(|path| path.file_name() == Some(row.target.as_str()))

  6917	    let digest = blake3::hash(&fs::read(&candidate)?).to_hex().to_string();
  6918	    require_eq(
  6919	        &format!("{} replayed sanitizer binary digest", row.target),
  6920	        &proof.binary_blake3,
  6921	        &digest,

  6926	        probe_text.contains(runtime_name),
  6927	        "replayed binary for {} does not carry the {} runtime ({runtime_name} absent from its help)",

  6932	}

  6934	fn find_named_files(root: &Utf8Path, name: &str) -> Result<Vec<Utf8PathBuf>> {
  6935	    let mut found = Vec::new();
  6936	    if !root.exists() {
  6937	        return Ok(found);
  6938	    }
  6939	    for entry in fs::read_dir(root)? {
  6940	        let entry = entry?;
  6941	        let path = Utf8PathBuf::from_path_buf(entry.path()).map_err(|path| {
  6942	            anyhow::anyhow!("non-UTF-8 path while finding {name}: {}", path.display())
  6943	        })?;
  6944	        if entry.file_type()?.is_dir() {
  6945	            found.extend(find_named_files(&path, name)?);
  6946	        } else if path.file_name() == Some(name) {
  6947	            found.push(path);
  6948	        }
  6949	    }
  6950	    Ok(found)
  6951	}

  6799	fn verify_sanitizer_build_replay(
  6800	    root: &Utf8Path,
  6801	    row: &FuzzEvidence,
  6802	    proof: &SanitizerProof,
  6803	    provenance: &Provenance,
  6804	) -> Result<()> {
  6805	    // Rebuild at the CANONICAL path the campaign built at (M17.5 F-42), not a
  6806	    // scratch worktree. Measured: the same commit built at two paths differs in
  6807	    // .rodata by its codegen-unit name, because cargo hashes the fuzz crate's
  6808	    // absolute manifest path into `-C metadata`; two clean builds at one fixed
  6809	    // path are byte-identical. The path and flags are closed here and the proof
  6810	    // must record the same, so neither side can drift from the other.
  6811	    let (build_root, build_rustflags) = sanitizer_build_canon(&provenance.fixed_commit);
  6812	    require_eq(
  6813	        &format!("{} sanitizer build_root", row.target),
  6814	        &proof.build_root,
  6815	        build_root.as_str(),
  6816	    )?;
  6817	    // The cargo-home remap's SOURCE is the campaign machine's $HOME and does
  6818	    // not shape a single byte -- its TARGET (/cargo) does. Comparing the raw
  6819	    // string would refuse a byte-identical build from any machine with a
  6820	    // different home directory (HEAD review). Compare with the source
  6821	    // normalized; the build-root remap and the cwd prefix must still match
  6822	    // exactly, because those DO determine the bytes.
  6823	    require_eq(
  6824	        &format!("{} sanitizer build_rustflags", row.target),
  6825	        &normalize_build_rustflags(&proof.build_rustflags),
  6826	        &normalize_build_rustflags(&build_rustflags),
  6827	    )?;
  6828	    // Hold a SHARED lock on the build base while this tree is in use: the
  6829	    // campaign prunes sibling commits' trees under an exclusive lock, so a
  6830	    // replay mid-build cannot have its worktree removed from under it (HEAD
  6831	    // review). std's File::lock_shared is stable on this toolchain.
  6832	    let base = build_root
  6833	        .parent()
  6834	        .context("canonical build root has a parent")?;
  6835	    fs::create_dir_all(base)?;
  6836	    let lock = fs::File::create(base.join(".lock")).context("open sanitizer build lock")?;
  6837	    lock.lock_shared()
  6838	        .context("shared-lock sanitizer build base")?;
  6839	    let worktree = build_root.clone();
  6840	    // A worktree is reusable only when the build's own inputs are THERE, not
  6841	    // merely when `.git` is. The checkout is `--no-checkout`, then
  6842	    // sparse-checkout, then checkout: interrupt it between those and `.git`
  6843	    // exists over a tree with no `crates/` and a `fuzz/` holding nothing but
  6844	    // the `.cargo` this function writes. Being an existence check on the wrong
  6845	    // file, the old condition then reused that forever, and every run failed
  6846	    // with "could not read the manifest file: .../fuzz/Cargo.toml" — which is
  6847	    // what a `just ci` killed mid-run left behind on 2026-09-20.
  6848	    //
  6849	    // The manifest is the right witness: it is exactly what `cargo fuzz build`
  6850	    // opens first, so if it is present the build can start, and if it is not
  6851	    // there is nothing to salvage.
  6852	    let usable = worktree.join(".git").exists() && worktree.join("fuzz/Cargo.toml").exists();
  6853	    if !usable {
  6854	        if worktree.exists() {
  6855	            // Registered-but-incomplete is the case that matters; `git worktree
  6856	            // add` refuses a path it still knows about, so drop the
  6857	            // registration with the directory.
  6858	            let _ = Command::new("git")
  6859	                .current_dir(root)
  6860	                .args(["worktree", "remove", "--force", worktree.as_str()])
  6861	                .status();
  6862	            if worktree.exists() {
  6863	                fs::remove_dir_all(&worktree).with_context(|| format!("clear stale {worktree}"))?;
  6864	            }
  6865	            let _ = Command::new("git")
  6866	                .current_dir(root)
  6867	                .args(["worktree", "prune"])
  6868	                .status();
  6869	        }
  6870	        if let Some(parent) = worktree.parent() {
  6871	            fs::create_dir_all(parent)?;
  6872	        }
  6873	        add_sparse_worktree(
  6874	            root,
  6875	            &worktree,
  6876	            &provenance.fixed_commit,
  6877	            "sanitizer replay",
  6878	        )?;
  6879	    }
  6880	    fs::create_dir_all(worktree.join("fuzz/.cargo"))?;
  6881	    fs::write(
  6882	        worktree.join("fuzz/.cargo/config.toml"),
  6883	        "[unstable]\ntrim-paths = true\n\n[profile.release]\ntrim-paths = \"all\"\n",
  6884	    )?;
  6885	    let output = Command::new("cargo")
  6886	        .current_dir(&worktree)
  6887	        .env("RUSTFLAGS", &build_rustflags)
  6888	        // Pin the target directory to the one the lookup below reads. Cargo
  6889	        // takes `build.target-dir` from `$CARGO_HOME/config.toml`, which is
  6890	        // outside this repository: when that key was added on 2026-09-18 the
  6891	        // build started landing in a shared tree and `find_named_files` saw an
  6892	        // empty `fuzz/target`. Worse than the failure is the success it can
  6893	        // fake — a binary another build left at this path would be hashed as
  6894	        // if this replay had produced it. The value restores cargo-fuzz's own
  6895	        // default, so recorded digests are unaffected.
  6896	        .env("CARGO_TARGET_DIR", worktree.join("fuzz/target"))
  6897	        .args([
  6898	            &format!("+{SANITIZER_TOOLCHAIN}"),
  6899	            "fuzz",
  6900	            "build",
  6901	            "-s",
  6902	            row.sanitizer.as_str(),
  6903	            row.target.as_str(),
  6904	        ])
  6905	        .output()
  6906	        .with_context(|| format!("replay sanitizer build for {}", row.target))?;
  6907	    anyhow::ensure!(
  6908	        output.status.success(),
  6909	        "replayed sanitizer build failed for {}: {}",
  6910	        row.target,
  6911	        String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr).trim()
  6912	    );
  6913	    let candidate = find_named_files(&worktree.join("fuzz/target"), &row.target)?
  6914	        .into_iter()
  6915	        .find(|path| path.file_name() == Some(row.target.as_str()))
  6916	        .with_context(|| format!("replayed sanitizer build produced no {} binary", row.target))?;
  6917	    let digest = blake3::hash(&fs::read(&candidate)?).to_hex().to_string();
  6918	    require_eq(
  6919	        &format!("{} replayed sanitizer binary digest", row.target),
  6920	        &proof.binary_blake3,
  6921	        &digest,
  6922	    )?;
  6923	    let (probe_bytes, runtime_name) = probe_sanitizer_runtime(&candidate, &worktree, row)?;
  6924	    let probe_text = String::from_utf8_lossy(&probe_bytes);
  6925	    anyhow::ensure!(
  6926	        probe_text.contains(runtime_name),
  6927	        "replayed binary for {} does not carry the {} runtime ({runtime_name} absent from its help)",
  6928	        row.target,
  6929	        row.sanitizer
  6930	    );
  6931	    Ok(())
  6932	}

  6934	fn find_named_files(root: &Utf8Path, name: &str) -> Result<Vec<Utf8PathBuf>> {
  6935	    let mut found = Vec::new();
  6936	    if !root.exists() {
  6937	        return Ok(found);
  6938	    }
  6939	    for entry in fs::read_dir(root)? {
  6940	        let entry = entry?;
  6941	        let path = Utf8PathBuf::from_path_buf(entry.path()).map_err(|path| {
  6942	            anyhow::anyhow!("non-UTF-8 path while finding {name}: {}", path.display())
  6943	        })?;
  6944	        if entry.file_type()?.is_dir() {
  6945	            found.extend(find_named_files(&path, name)?);
  6946	        } else if path.file_name() == Some(name) {
  6947	            found.push(path);
  6948	        }
  6949	    }
  6950	    Ok(found)
  6951	}

  6975	fn verify_fuzz_log_metrics(row: &FuzzEvidence, bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<()> {
  6976	    let text = String::from_utf8_lossy(bytes);
  6977	    let stat_execs = text
  6978	        .lines()
  6979	        .filter_map(|line| line.strip_prefix("stat::number_of_executed_units:"))
  6980	        .next_back()
  6981	        .and_then(|value| value.trim().parse::<u64>().ok())
  6982	        .with_context(|| {
  6983	            format!(
  6984	                "{}: retained fuzz log has no execution-count footer",
  6985	                row.target
  6986	            )
  6987	        })?;
  6988	    require_eq(
  6989	        &format!("{} log execution count", row.target),
  6990	        &stat_execs.to_string(),
  6991	        &row.execs.to_string(),
  6992	    )?;
  6993	    let done = text
  6994	        .lines()
  6995	        .filter_map(|line| line.strip_prefix("Done "))
  6996	        .next_back()
  6997	        .with_context(|| format!("{}: retained fuzz log has no Done footer", row.target))?;
  6998	    let done_execs = done
  6999	        .split_whitespace()
  7000	        .next()
  7001	        .and_then(|value| value.parse::<u64>().ok())
  7002	        .with_context(|| format!("{}: malformed Done execution count", row.target))?;
  7003	    let done_elapsed = done
  7004	        .split(" in ")
  7005	        .nth(1)
  7006	        .and_then(|value| value.split_whitespace().next())
  7007	        .and_then(|value| value.parse::<u64>().ok())
  7008	        .with_context(|| format!("{}: malformed Done elapsed seconds", row.target))?;
  7009	    anyhow::ensure!(
  7010	        done_execs == row.execs,
  7011	        "{}: log Done count {} differs from evidence {}",

  7244	/// pair of paid model reviews inside every lane, and it threatened §7's
  7245	/// eight-hour ceiling with work that produced no new evidence.

  7248	/// Populating it — which `verify_corpus_scope_presence` requires — would have
  7249	/// switched it on.

  7252	/// lane captures each scope under strace as it actually runs, and the gate
  7253	/// checks the recorded bytes: the command matches the closed lane registry, the
  7254	/// path digest matches, no stage wrote to the repository's locked corpus and no
  7255	/// carved fuzz binary touched it at all (F-44 ruling, 2026-09-05), and every

  7271	            &format!("{} corpus scope command", row.scope),

  7494	/// prints one syscall per line, so the earliest needle is the line's call.

  7502	/// Whether strace reported a failed syscall. Inspect only the return-value
  7503	/// delimiter after the final syscall close, so a valid filename containing
  7504	/// the text ` = -1 ` cannot masquerade as an `ENOENT` result.
  7505	fn scope_trace_line_failed(line: &str) -> bool {
  7506	    line.rfind(") = ")
  7507	        .and_then(|index| line[index + 4..].split_whitespace().next())
  7508	        .is_some_and(|value| value == "-1")

  7511	/// The same, plus the directory fd each path was resolved against: the nearest
  7512	/// preceding bare integer argument, `None` for `AT_FDCWD` and for calls that
  7513	/// take no dirfd. Blind pass 1 at 5fb1b57 (A10, A11): only `openat`'s FIRST
  7514	/// argument was read, so `renameat`'s destination dirfd was ignored and a
  7515	/// descriptor opened without `O_DIRECTORY` was dropped from the map entirely.
  7516	fn scope_trace_line_arguments(line: &str) -> Vec<(String, bool, Option<i64>)> {
  7517	    let Some((open, needle)) = FILE_SYSCALLS
  7518	        .into_iter()
  7519	        .filter_map(|needle| line.find(needle).map(|index| (index, needle)))
  7520	        .min_by_key(|(index, _)| *index)
  7521	    else {
  7522	        return Vec::new();
  7523	    };
  7524	    let rest = &line[open..];
  7525	    let write = WRITE_SYSCALLS.contains(&needle)
  7526	        || (OPEN_SYSCALLS.contains(&needle)
  7527	            && OPEN_WRITE_FLAGS.iter().any(|flag| rest.contains(flag)));
  7528	    let wanted = if TWO_PATH_SYSCALLS.contains(&needle) {
  7529	        2
  7530	    } else {
  7531	        1
  7532	    };
  7533	    let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(wanted);
  7534	    // The argument list, past the syscall name: without this the text before a
  7535	    // path reads `openat(7`, whose last comma-separated piece is the name
  7536	    // glued to the fd and parses as nothing.
  7537	    let args = &rest[needle.len()..];
  7538	    let mut cursor = args;
  7539	    let mut consumed = 0usize;
  7540	    for _ in 0..wanted {
  7541	        let Some(start) = cursor.find('"') else { break };
  7542	        let Some(end) = cursor[start + 1..].find('"') else {
  7543	            break;
  7544	        };
  7545	        let dirfd = args[..consumed + start]
  7546	            .rsplit(',')
  7547	            .find_map(|argument| argument.trim().parse::<i64>().ok());
  7548	        out.push((cursor[start + 1..start + 1 + end].to_owned(), write, dirfd));
  7549	        consumed += start + 1 + end + 1;
  7550	        cursor = &cursor[start + 1 + end + 1..];
  7551	    }
  7552	    out
  7553	}

  7617	fn anchor_relative_paths(

  7630	            .and_then(|fd| open_fds.get(&(pid, fd)))
  7631	            .or_else(|| cwds.get(&pid))

  7634	        }
  7635	    }

  7650	/// The (source, duplicate) descriptor pair a successful `dup`, `dup2`, `dup3`

  7655	/// anchored against nothing. A duplicate names what its source named.
  7656	fn record_duplicated_fd(

  7660	    open_fds: &mut BTreeMap<(u32, i64), String>,

  7252	/// lane captures each scope under strace as it actually runs, and the gate
  7253	/// checks the recorded bytes: the command matches the closed lane registry, the
  7254	/// path digest matches, no stage wrote to the repository's locked corpus and no

  7493	/// because a link INTO the locked corpus is the second-name attack. strace
  7494	/// prints one syscall per line, so the earliest needle is the line's call.
  7495	fn scope_trace_line_accesses(line: &str) -> Vec<(String, bool)> {

  7502	/// Whether strace reported a failed syscall. Inspect only the return-value
  7503	/// delimiter after the final syscall close, so a valid filename containing
  7504	/// the text ` = -1 ` cannot masquerade as an `ENOENT` result.
  7505	fn scope_trace_line_failed(line: &str) -> bool {
  7506	    line.rfind(") = ")

  7508	        .is_some_and(|value| value == "-1")

  7511	/// The same, plus the directory fd each path was resolved against: the nearest
  7512	/// preceding bare integer argument, `None` for `AT_FDCWD` and for calls that
  7513	/// take no dirfd. Blind pass 1 at 5fb1b57 (A10, A11): only `openat`'s FIRST
  7514	/// argument was read, so `renameat`'s destination dirfd was ignored and a
  7515	/// descriptor opened without `O_DIRECTORY` was dropped from the map entirely.
  7516	fn scope_trace_line_arguments(line: &str) -> Vec<(String, bool, Option<i64>)> {
  7517	    let Some((open, needle)) = FILE_SYSCALLS
  7518	        .into_iter()
  7519	        .filter_map(|needle| line.find(needle).map(|index| (index, needle)))
  7520	        .min_by_key(|(index, _)| *index)
  7521	    else {
  7522	        return Vec::new();
  7523	    };
  7524	    let rest = &line[open..];
  7525	    let write = WRITE_SYSCALLS.contains(&needle)
  7526	        || (OPEN_SYSCALLS.contains(&needle)
  7527	            && OPEN_WRITE_FLAGS.iter().any(|flag| rest.contains(flag)));
  7528	    let wanted = if TWO_PATH_SYSCALLS.contains(&needle) {
  7529	        2
  7530	    } else {
  7531	        1
  7532	    };
  7533	    let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(wanted);
  7534	    // The argument list, past the syscall name: without this the text before a
  7535	    // path reads `openat(7`, whose last comma-separated piece is the name
  7536	    // glued to the fd and parses as nothing.
  7537	    let args = &rest[needle.len()..];
  7538	    let mut cursor = args;
  7539	    let mut consumed = 0usize;
  7540	    for _ in 0..wanted {
  7541	        let Some(start) = cursor.find('"') else { break };
  7542	        let Some(end) = cursor[start + 1..].find('"') else {
  7543	            break;
  7544	        };
  7545	        let dirfd = args[..consumed + start]
  7546	            .rsplit(',')
  7547	            .find_map(|argument| argument.trim().parse::<i64>().ok());
  7548	        out.push((cursor[start + 1..start + 1 + end].to_owned(), write, dirfd));
  7549	        consumed += start + 1 + end + 1;
  7550	        cursor = &cursor[start + 1 + end + 1..];
  7551	    }
  7552	    out
  7553	}

  7630	            .and_then(|fd| open_fds.get(&(pid, fd)))

  7650	/// The (source, duplicate) descriptor pair a successful `dup`, `dup2`, `dup3`

  7652	/// the return value.
  7653	/// Blind pass 1 at 9eca4f0 (A07): only open-derived descriptors were tracked,
  7654	/// so `dup`ing a locked directory fd and writing through the duplicate
  7655	/// anchored against nothing. A duplicate names what its source named.
  7656	fn record_duplicated_fd(
  7657	    line: &str,
  7658	    pid: u32,
  7659	    returned_fd: Option<i64>,
  7660	    open_fds: &mut BTreeMap<(u32, i64), String>,
  7661	) {
  7662	    if let Some((from, to)) = duplicated_fd(line, returned_fd)
  7663	        && let Some(dir) = open_fds.get(&(pid, from)).cloned()
  7664	    {

  7666	    }

  7669	fn duplicated_fd(line: &str, returned_fd: Option<i64>) -> Option<(i64, i64)> {
  7670	    let to = returned_fd.filter(|fd| *fd >= 0)?;
  7671	    let call = ["dup(", "dup2(", "dup3(", "fcntl("]
  7672	        .into_iter()
  7673	        .find(|name| line.contains(name))?;
  7674	    if call == "fcntl(" && !line.contains("F_DUPFD") {
  7675	        return None;
  7676	    }
  7677	    // strace prints these as `dup2(3, 7) = 7` — integer arguments only, so the
  7678	    // first comma-separated piece is the source descriptor.
  7679	    let args = line.split_once(call)?.1;
  7680	    let from = args
  7681	        .split(',')
  7682	        .next()?
  7683	        .trim_end_matches(')')
  7684	        .trim()
  7685	        .parse::<i64>()
  7686	        .ok()?;
  7687	    Some((from, to))
  7688	}

<!-- Canonical instructions. ~/.codex/AGENTS.md and ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md
     link here. Edit this file, not vendor-generated copies. -->

# Code navigation

- Use `rg` for current text and `ast-grep` for syntax patterns.
- Use Serena for narrow symbol/reference queries in the exact checkout.
- Use `code-search -l 'repo:NAME QUERY'` for Zoekt search of committed HEAD.
  Verify results against working-tree files. Refresh with `code-index zoekt`.
- SCIP exports are snapshots, not live authority. Index on demand, never as
  a commit gate. Commands: `/mnt/4tb/code-intelligence/README.md`.

# Review policy

Mandatory model reviews are suspended for all projects. This owner decision
supersedes older per-commit, feature-batch, and automatic model-review rules
in repository instructions. Use model review only when explicitly requested.
Unavailable review tools do not block ordinary work.

Continue code inspection, tests, linting, and relevant runtime checks. Preserve
independent release gates, human review, and authorization requirements.
Verify external findings against source or a reproduction before fixing them.

# Shared resources

- Preserve unrelated edits. Use separate worktrees for concurrent writers.
- Separate MCP processes and sandbox namespaces can still share files and
  backend services. Inspect ownership before changing routing or stopping services.
- Confirm recovery scope and user authorization before destructive rollback.
- Keep secrets out of source and logs, and never write one to disk in
  plaintext. API keys live encrypted in `~/.config/secrets/keys.enc.env`
  (sops + age, TPM-unlocked; recovery key in Bitwarden). Add a key with
  `secrets set NAME` (value on stdin); run anything that needs keys as
  `secrets run -- CMD`. Refer to keys by environment name only.

# Optional LAMU and Katana

For LAMU delegation, routing, Katana execution, budgets, or session recovery,
read `/home/brianklam/.codex/skills/lamu-katana-workflow/SKILL.md`.
Use these tools when they benefit the task, not as mandatory steps.

# Memory

- Index entries (`MEMORY.md`) are pointers, not summaries: one line, hook
  under ~120 characters. Detail belongs in the linked file.
- Replace stale content; never append `Prior (sha):` chains or revision
  history. Git log is the authority for history; memory holds current state.
- Record only what code and git cannot tell you: decisions, constraints,
  reversals and their reasons, owed work.
